## CI - Weekly dependency report in a pinned issue (2026-11-03, ci)

- **What:** `.github/workflows/dependency-report.yml` runs every Monday and on demand, and rewrites the single open issue labelled `dependency-report` ([#148](https://github.com/thiennd212/AqtCoreFW/issues/148)). Sections: CVE (NuGet `--vulnerable --include-transitive`, `pnpm audit`), licence changed to commercial (`scripts/dependency-report/license-watchlist.json`: MediatR, MassTransit, FluentAssertions with replacement options; QuestPDF watched), version mismatch between `src/` and `tests/` props, major, minor/patch, .NET SDK against the release index, pinned Docker images and GitHub Actions.
- **Scope:** read-only; no file edits, no pull requests. Permissions `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` only. Upgrades are handed to Claude per issue section; see `docs/ops/dependency-report-runbook.md`.
- **First report (2026-11-03):** NuGet 0 vulnerable packages; web 13 critical / 52 high advisories across 18 packages (orval, seroval, axios among them); FluentAssertions 8.2.0 already under the commercial licence; MediatR 12.5.0 and MassTransit 8.3.6 on their last free majors; `Testcontainers.MsSql` and `Testcontainers.Redis` 4.4.0 in `src/` vs 3.10.0 in `tests/`; SDK pin 10.0.103 vs channel 10.0.403.
- **Verification:** `node --test scripts/dependency-report/tests/*.test.mjs` 16/16; actionlint and shellcheck clean; local run created, pinned and updated issue #148, and a second resolve returned the same issue.

## Chore - CI runs only where it buys evidence (2026-11-03, ci)

- **Why:** the repo is private on a fixed free Actions budget that will not be raised. Every PR ran CI twice (PR and push to `main`, about 30 billed minutes each), and PRs #142-#145 hit the spending limit so their jobs never started.
- **Change:** `ci.yml` starts on a PR only for high-risk backend paths (build and package config, migrations, shared kernel, hosts, identity, audit, Semgrep rules, CI itself) and on `main` only for backend paths. The frontend job moved to `ci-frontend.yml` with its own paths. Draft PRs skip CI. New `scripts/check-before-merge.sh` runs the matching local build and tests for PRs that do not start CI.
- **Docs:** policy table in `docs/deployment-guide.md` section 0 ("When CI runs"); references updated in `frontend-code-standards.md`, `ops/ci-smoke-gate-runbook.md`, `tech-stack.md`.

## Security - Introspection client secret fails closed outside dev (2026-11-03, identity)

- **Problem:** `Auth:ResourceClientSecret` had a literal fallback in `IdentityInfrastructureRegistration` and AuthServer seeded the `aqtcorefw-api-resource` client with the same literal in every environment, and no config set the key. Every deployment used a secret that is public in the repository, so anyone with the repo could call `/connect/introspect`.
- **Fix:** `AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure.Configuration.AuthResourceClient` resolves the secret; the dev value is allowed only in Development/Testing/Benchmark, otherwise a missing or dev value fails startup. `ProductionSecretValidator` requires the key and rejects the dev value. AuthServer seeds the client with the configured secret and rotates an existing client whose stored secret differs.
- **Breaking for deployments:** set `Auth__ResourceClientSecret` in Vault `secret/aqtcorefw` before rolling out (AuthServer first, then Api); see `deployment-guide.md`. `scripts/k8s-local-generate-prod-secrets.sh` seeds it for fresh local clusters. `deployment-guide.md` key names corrected (`OpenIddict__ClientSecret` was stale).
- **Docs:** `code-standards.md` adds the "client secrets with a dev default" rule and the startup-seeder exception to `Cross-Module Data Access`.
- **Verification:** `AqtCoreFW.Architecture.Tests` 211/211, `Infrastructure.Extensions.Tests` 236 (1 skip), `Identity.Infrastructure.Tests` 348, `Startup.SmokeTests` 31. Not covered by a test: the rotation branch on an existing database.

## Fix - Docker compose runs on a fresh volume and on arm64 (2026-10-29, dev-env)

- **Images:** `src/host/AqtCoreFW.Api/Dockerfile` and `AuthServer/Dockerfile` pick the RID from the build machine (`linux-musl-arm64` or `linux-musl-x64`) instead of a hard-coded `linux-musl-x64`, which stamped x64 assemblies that an arm64 runtime could not load (exit 139). AuthServer's `appuser` now has a home directory so Development-mode dev certificates can be written to the X509 store.
- **Compose:** `minio/minio` is no longer pullable from Docker Hub (denied for every tag, no quay.io manifest); compose and `infra/k8s-local/minio.yaml` now use `ghcr.io/coollabsio/minio:RELEASE.2025-10-15T17-29-55Z` (amd64 + arm64). Web healthcheck calls `127.0.0.1` (busybox `wget` resolved `localhost` to `::1`, nginx listens on IPv4 only). `authserver` waits for a healthy `sqlserver` and `api` waits for a healthy `authserver`, so both no longer race on `CREATE DATABASE` (SQL error 1801). AuthServer's connection string adds `PoolBlockingPeriod=NeverBlock` so a login failure before the first migration is not replayed after the database exists. `api` gets `ConnectionStrings__AuditAdmin` pointing at `sqlserver`; `appsettings.Development.json` points it at `localhost`, which kept `/health/ready` at 503 in the container.
- **Docs:** README links Scalar (`/scalar/v1`, `/openapi/v1.json`) instead of the removed Swagger UI; unused `Swashbuckle.AspNetCore` central version removed.
- **Verification:** `docker compose up -d --build` on Apple Silicon (arm64) from empty volumes: all services healthy, `/.well-known/openid-configuration` 200, `/scalar/v1` 200, `/openapi/v1.json` 200, `/swagger` 404, `/health/ready` 200. Not run on x64.
- **macOS port 5000:** AirPlay Receiver holds host port 5000, so the authserver mapping is now `${AUTH_PORT:-5000}`, and `Auth__IssuerUri`, `Auth__AuthorityUrl` and the web `VITE_OIDC_AUTHORITY` build arg follow it. Copy the example env file in `infra/docker/` and set `AUTH_PORT` (e.g. 5100). `infra/docker/smoke-test.sh` still probes 5000.

## Security - Pin System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13 (2026-10-15, deps)

- GHSA-846f-f764-76mx (high) and GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7 (moderate), published 2026-10-13, cover the transitive `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 9.0.4 / 10.0.0 the solution resolved. NuGet audit turned them into restore errors under the Release `/warnaserror` build, so CI `unit-tests` failed for every change.
- Central transitive pin to the first patched 10.0.13 in `src/` and `tests/` `Directory.Packages.props`. Verified: `dotnet list package --vulnerable` reports no vulnerable project in `ci/unit.slnx`; `ci/unit.slnx` Release `/warnaserror` build 0 warnings; `src/AqtCoreFW.slnx` and `ci/integration.slnx` build; unit tests 4,637 passed across 41 assemblies.

## Fix - Storage download integrity + tenant user seed lands on target (2026-10-15, files/identity)

- **Files:** `MinioFileStorageService.DownloadAsync` now throws `IOException` when the bytes read differ from the HEAD size. Minio SDK 6.0.4 does not throw when the GET is refused (403 AccessDenied while HEAD is allowed); it passed the S3 error XML to the callback, so downloads returned the XML with HTTP 200 and the ClamAV scan certified it clean (seen on the v26grdnb63 dev environment). The scan job now fails and Hangfire retries, leaving the file Quarantined. Minio 7.0.0 throws `AccessDeniedException` for the same response; upgrading is a separate decision.
- **Identity:** `TenantUserSeeder` tops up the Pass 2 integer-division remainder round-robin so each tenant lands exactly on `UserCount` (BNV 1,500 was 1,498). Below target, every startup took the drift path and wiped + re-seeded the tenant's users. BTC (exact split) output is unchanged. This reverses the 2026-06-01 "truncation preserved, no action" note now that the legacy seeder is gone.
- **Tests:** `MinioFileStorageServiceDownloadTests` (loopback S3 stub: refused GET throws, allowed GET returns the object); `TenantUserSeederTests` asserts the exact target, no re-seed on the second run, and faker reproducibility through a forced drift re-seed.

## Feature — Forms cascade H2: Vault-authed external DS + reject-on-public guard (FORMS-CASCADE-PUBLIC-EXTERNAL-INROW) (2026-08-06, forms/security)

- **Branch:** `feat/forms-cascade-public-external-inrow` — H2 slice = Phase-04 `8fd6ad4b2` (Vault-authed fetch) + Phase-05 `4e0bf9f68` (reject-on-public guard). Pushed bitbucket + origin (NOT merged main — feature-branch per v1 pattern, awaits M1). Post-v1.0 gated feature under user override.
- **Phase-04 (What):** External data sources gain optional Vault-managed API-key auth. Config `AuthMode` (null=static/backward | "Bearer" | custom-header) + `VaultKeyId` + `HeaderName`. `ExternalDataSourceAuthKeyResolver` (optional `IVaultClient`, fail-closed, no legacy fallback) reads `secret/aqt/forms/external-ds/{vaultKeyId}/api-key`, 5-min IMemoryCache. Per-request `HttpRequestMessage` so the auth header never pollutes the shared named client. SSRF guards run BEFORE auth resolution. 6 unit tests.
- **Phase-05 (What):** Publish/Republish now REJECT a public form (`IsPublic=1`) carrying a Vault-authed external DS — GOV_FRM_044. Closes the C1×H2 intersection: the anonymous options endpoint uses the same resolver, so without the guard an authed-external config on a public form would issue a Vault-authed outbound fetch on behalf of an unauthenticated caller. `CascadeDependencyValidator.EnsureNoAuthedExternalOnPublic` iterates ALL active fields (anonymous endpoint has no top-level filter → in-row child authed-external is reachable too). Private forms unaffected.
- **Security fix caught in review (blocking):** the guard parses `AuthMode` with the SAME System.Text.Json deserializer the resolver uses (local mirror `record` + case-insensitive options, last-property-wins) — a first draft's hand-rolled `JsonDocument` walk was first-property-wins, so a duplicate-key craft `{"AuthMode":"","AuthMode":"Bearer"}` bypassed the guard yet authenticated at runtime. Unparseable/non-string AuthMode now fails closed (rejects publish; also prevents an anonymous 500 from an unhandled JsonException).
- **Tests:** Forms.Domain 192/192 (+3 net adversarial: dup-key, number-typed, child-field), Publish/Republish handlers 33/33, Infrastructure 0-warn. Journals `journal-260805-1600-forms-cascade-h2-vault-authed-external.md` + `journal-260806-1606-forms-cascade-h2-phase05-reject-authed-external-public.md`. C1 (anonymous public cascade) shipped earlier same branch (`ec36c3e22`+`4f1c9bdb7`+`5976aa2f0`). M1 (in-row TableField cascade) remains open. New SSRF-hardening row `FORMS-EXTERNAL-DS-IPV6-LITERAL-SSRF-GAP` filed post-v1.0.

## Feature — Forms cross-field cascading data-source v1 slice (FORMS-CASCADING-DATASOURCE) (2026-08-05, forms)

- **Branch:** `feat/forms-cascading-datasource` commit `95b6a120c` (NOT merged to main / not pushed — feature-branch-only per user; feature is post-v1.0 gated, shipped under explicit user override).
- **What:** A child form field's option-list is filtered by one-or-more PARENT fields' selected values. Schema: `DataSourceJson.dependencies:[{dependsOnFieldKey, filterParamName}]` (empty/absent = old static path = backward-safe discriminator). v1 scope = AUTHED-only, TOP-LEVEL fields, External-static + keyed-Enum.
- **BE:** `IDataSourceResolver.ResolveAsync` +optional `parentValues` (3 impls; Internal accepts-ignores per red-team H1). NEW `CascadeDependencyValidator` (Forms.Domain) — Kahn topo-sort cycle + self-dep + dangling-ref at `FormTemplate.Publish/Republish`, plus `EnsureNotDependedOn` reject-delete guard in `DeactivateField` (GOV_FRM_040-043). `ExternalDataSourceResolver`: parent values appended via `Uri.GetComponents`+`Uri.EscapeDataString` (NOT `UriBuilder.Query` — it mangles pre-escaped values); cache-key parent-aware, byte-identical when no parents. `EnumDataSourceResolver`: config-driven `parentFilterMap` (parentValue → allowed enum values), multi-parent intersection, fail-safe-empty when unmapped. `GetFormFieldOptionsQuery` +optional `ParentValues`; endpoint `GET .../fields/{fieldId}/options` +`[FromQuery] p[key]=value`, stays class `[Authorize]`.
- **FE:** `useFieldOptions(+parentValues,+enabled)` (parentValues in query-key → auto-refetch on parent change). `RefFieldSelect` watches parents, gates fetch until all-parents-set, clears stale child on parent change (clear-propagation + first-watch edit-flow guard). Builder `CascadeDependenciesEditor` + `EnumParentFilterMapEditor` (keyed-Enum map authoring) + soft client cycle-warn. Pure helpers `cascade-dependencies.ts` + `cascade-builder.ts`.
- **Deferred (red-team C1/H1/H2/M1 → backlog `FORMS-CASCADE-PUBLIC-EXTERNAL-INROW`):** anonymous-public cascade, external-Vault-auth, Internal-multi-param, in-row TableField.
- **Tests:** BE 617/617 (Domain 185 +7 / App 378 +3 / Infra 54 +13), FE forms 204/204 (+30). Review 8.5/10, 0 critical (3 findings addressed). Caught+fixed a real `UriBuilder.Query` escape-mangle bug. 8-phase TDD cook, plan `260804-1701-*`, journal `journal-260805-forms-cascading-datasource-v1.md`.

## Fix — Forms submit-time Formula JsonElement→CLR normalize gap + DRY consolidation (FORMS-SUBMIT-PREPROCESSOR-JSONELEMENT-NCALC-GAP) (2026-08-04, forms)

**Type:** fix (post-v1.0, DRY debt) · branch `fix/forms-preprocessor-jsonelement-ncalc-gap` · Forms.Application 375/375 unit + Forms integration 9/9 · code-review APPROVE-WITH-NITS 8.5/10 (0 crit/high).

- **Problem:** Three redundant JsonElement→CLR normalizations existed across the codebase (`JsonValueNormalizer` canonical + `FormulaBatchEvaluator.NormalizeJsonElementScalars` from Phase-4A + `FormDataPreprocessor.JsonElementToObject` submit-time). FormDataPreprocessor submit Formula path wasn't using the P1 normalization discovered at endpoint-time, leaving JsonElement scalars to fail NCalc arithmetic (silent null degrade). DRY violation.
- **Fix:** Consolidated all three conversion points onto `JsonValueNormalizer` canonical. Deleted 2 private copies. FormDataPreprocessor.PreprocessDataAsync Formula branch now normalizes `rawData` via `JsonValueNormalizer.NormalizeDict()` before IFormulaEvaluationService.EvaluateAsync. ParseTableFieldRows and DeserializeJsonRow repoint to canonical. Graceful semantic delta: canonical adds double fallback for |x|>7.9e28 (old private version threw; canonical is strict improvement for gov data). Table-cell audit verified only scalar SQL types stored (no nested Array/Object reachable), so recursive capability of canonical is benign-overhead vs. bounds the surface for future.
- **Verification:** Ground-truth corrected the backlog premise (3 bans, not 1). Both 2A+2B repoint targets validated regression-free. Code-review caught and verified as non-blocking both backward-deltas (type upgrades, malformed-input paths).

## Feature — Dynamic Forms Phase-4A: Formula Compute End-to-End (BE evaluate endpoint + reactive FE) (2026-08-04, forms)

**Type:** feature (Forms flagship polish) · PR #136 squash `c7db73e9c` · plan `260804-1245-forms-phase4a-formula-compute-endpoint` · BE 15 tests + FE 15 tests · Debug+Release `/warnaserror` 0W · code-review APPROVE-WITH-NITS 9.4/10 (0 crit/high/med, 5 red-team axes PASS). Closes backlog `FORMS-HARDENING-PHASE3-4` (last sub-part).

- **What:** Formula fields now display real computed values reactively during fill, both authenticated and public. Reuses the live 2A sandbox (`FormulaEvaluationService`) via a shared `FormulaBatchEvaluator` — **one eval engine, no client-side JS eval** (locked decision, DRY).
- **BE authed:** `POST /api/v1/forms/templates/{publicId}/evaluate-formulas` (`[Authorize]` class-level, tenant-scoped, `authenticated` rate-limit). Body `{ values }` → `{ results: { fieldKey: computedValue } }` for every active Formula field. Read-only compute, writes nothing.
- **BE public:** `POST /api/v1/public/forms/{code}/evaluate-formulas` (`[AllowAnonymous]`, TenantId server-derived from Code via `public_forms_bypass`, no client tenant param). New rate-limit policy `formula-evaluate` (dev 300 / prod 30 per IP/min), synced across all 5 config sites.
- **FE:** `useEvaluateFormulas` / `useEvaluatePublicFormulas` hooks + `use-debounced-value` + `use-formula-values` (watch-all + 300ms debounce). Formula field renders computed value display-only via `Input value=` (never `setFieldsValue` → no feedback loop). Left name-unbound: antd `Form.Item` `name` overrides `value=`, and `cleanFormData` already strips Formula from submit.
- **Bug caught by integration test (would false-green on mock-only unit):** ASP.NET binds `Dictionary<string,object?>` numeric scalars as `JsonElement`; NCalc 6.1.1 throws on boxed-JsonElement arithmetic → sandbox catch-all → silent null. Fixed by normalizing JsonElement→CLR inside `FormulaBatchEvaluator` (verified via isolated NCalc repro). Submit-time `FormDataPreprocessor` shares the same latent gap → filed follow-up `FORMS-SUBMIT-PREPROCESSOR-JSONELEMENT-NCALC-GAP` (post-v1.0, graceful degrade).
- **Additive-only:** 0 migration, 0 schema change; `FormDataPreprocessor` submit path UNCHANGED (submit tests green).

## Feature — Forms Orphan Workflow-Link Retry (Phase 04+05+06+07: Hangfire Job + Admin API + FE Admin Page + Historical Backfill) (2026-08-04, forms)

**Type:** feature (launch-safety + operational reliability) · BE commits `ce07910d6` (job) + `de176756a` (admin API) · FE Phase 06 route + feature dir + i18n · Phase 07 backfill script + runbook + integration test · Forms.Infrastructure 56/56 + Forms.Application 179/179 + Architecture 149/149 · build 0E. All phases SHIPPED; completes plan `260803-2219-forms-orphan-workflow-link-retry`.

- **Problem:** Forms submissions that fail mid-transition to Workflow (after form validation, before/during WorkflowInstance.CreateAsync) leave orphaned `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingAttempt` rows in Pending status forever. No auto-retry, no admin visibility, no way to rescue the link without manual DBA intervention. Affects users whose submissions "appeared accepted" but never entered the workflow.
- **Phase 04 — Hangfire recurring job (`ce07910d6`):** `FormWorkflowLinkRetryJob` (Forms.Infrastructure/Jobs) registered via `AddRecurringJob("forms-workflow-link-retry", …)` in Program.cs at the same Testing flag gate as peer jobs. Runs every 5 minutes (cron `*/5`). **Core M1 idempotency:** resolves-before-create via `IWorkflowModuleClient.TryResolveInstanceForEntityAsync` (checks if workflow instance already exists for the submission) BEFORE calling `CreateInstanceAsync` — skips duplicate creation on retry. Claims due rows cross-tenant (`FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingAttemptRepository.GetDueAttemptsAsync`, new repo method), pins RLS per-row via `ICrossModuleUnitOfWork.BeginAsync(tenant)` for atomic state mutation + outbox enqueue (Forms→Workflow link event). Exponential backoff (5m → 10m → 20m … 6h max), shelves to Dead status at `MaxAttempts=10`. **New entities:** 6 lifecycle mutators on `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingAttempt` (domain methods: `IncrementAttempt`, `MarkSucceeded`, `MarkShelved`, `ResetNextRetryAt`). **New config:** `Forms:WorkflowLinkRetry` section (backoff curve, max-attempts). **Zero schema change:** the entity + migration `20260522144724` + tenant/status/retry indexes already shipped in phase 03 (backlog row `FORM-ORPHAN-WORKFLOW-LINK` materialized the entity contract pre-job).
- **Phase 05 — Admin API (`de176756a`):** NEW controller `WorkflowLinkPendingController` at `api/v1/forms/workflow-link-pending`. **3 endpoints:**
  - `GET ""` (paged Dapper list, tenant-scoped, all 4 statuses): `ListPendingWorkflowLinksQuery` + handler + `PendingWorkflowLinkListItemDto { submissionId, formTemplateId, status, nextRetryAt, attemptCount, lastAttemptAt }` (DTO-layer Dapper projection).
  - `POST {submissionId:guid}/retry` (202 Accepted, re-arms `NextRetryAt` = now + 5m, un-shelves Shelved rows): `RetryWorkflowLinkNowCommand` (idempotent re-arm, no duplicate trigger) + handler returns 202. Job stays the only create path (admin retry is just un-blocking the job).
  - `POST {submissionId:guid}/shelve` (202 Accepted, terminalize to Dead): `ShelveWorkflowLinkCommand` + handler. Blocks further retry attempts admin-side.
- **New permission:** `FORMS.WFLINK.MANAGE` (least-privilege admin capability; seeded in `E2ETestDataSeeder.Permissions.cs`; granted to Admin + SystemAdmin roles by default).
- **Zero new cross-module client method:** retries use the existing `IWorkflowModuleClient.TryResolveInstanceForEntityAsync` (shipped Phase 04, re-idempotency guard). Zero new entity/DbContext (table pre-existed Phase 03).

## Fix — Forms Table RLS Policy + Write-Path Tenant Pin (FORMS-WFLINK-PENDING-TABLE-NO-DB-RLS) (2026-08-04, forms)

**Type:** fix (data security + operational reliability) · migration `20260804030737_AddWorkflowLinkPendingAttemptRls` · `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingEventHandler` tenant-pin fix in Forms.Application · Forms.Infrastructure 56/56 + Forms.Application 179/179 · Architecture RLS test matrix 51/51 (`RlsPolicyPresenceTests`).

- **Problem:** `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingAttempts` table (shipped Phase 03, backlog `FORM-ORPHAN-WORKFLOW-LINK`) had no RLS policy, unlike all other Forms entities. When the retry job processes rows cross-tenant via `ICrossModuleUnitOfWork.BeginAsync(tenant)`, the write path was protected; however the event handler consuming public-form submissions (null ambient tenant context) would fail INSERT with SQL error 33504 (RLS BLOCK-AFTER-INSERT violation) once the policy was added, because the public endpoint has no explicit tenant binding.
- **Fix Part A — RLS Policy (migration `20260804030737_AddWorkflowLinkPendingAttemptRls`):** Added standard FILTER+BLOCK RLS predicate on TenantId column via `RlsMigrationHelper.GenerateRlsPolicyStatements()`. Table now covered under full tenant isolation, +1 to RLS policy count (51 total).
- **Fix Part B — Write-Path Tenant Pin (`FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingEventHandler`):** Handler now opens its own scoped `ICrossModuleUnitOfWork.BeginAsync(notification.TenantId)` around the read+insert operation, establishing explicit tenant context before any DB write. This ensures the BLOCK-AFTER-INSERT predicate sees a bound SESSION_CONTEXT TenantId matching the row's TenantId, preventing the 33504 error on public-form submissions. Retry job already pinned per row; db_owner backfill bypasses RLS. Enforcement verified by new `FormWorkflowLinkPendingRlsEnforcementTests` (non-db_owner) covering the public-form path.

## Feature — Dynamic Forms Phase-2 2A: Formula-eval DoS sandbox (2026-07-29, forms)

**Type:** feature (launch-safety) · commit `3206528ea` · Forms unit App 350/350 + Infrastructure 41/41 (8 new sandbox tests) + Domain 153/153 · Api host + Forms.Integration build 0-error. Closes Forms Phase-2 (2A+2B+2C+2D) → **HARD GATE (Forms vs 5 `[blocks-v1.0]`) now due before Phase 3-4.**

- **Mechanism:** `FormulaEvaluationService` now isolates each NCalc eval behind a process-wide static `SemaphoreSlim(N=Environment.ProcessorCount)` run in `Task.Run`, with a caller-side `WaitAsync(1000ms)` returning null on timeout. The permit is released **on eval-task completion via `ContinueWith`**, NOT in the caller's finally — releasing on caller-timeout would free the permit while the abandoned CPU-bound eval still runs, defeating the cap. Cancellation cannot abort an in-flight NCalc eval, so **isolation, not cancellation, is the guarantee**: a malicious eval is abandoned but concurrent abandonment stays capped at N regardless of request concurrency, so the request threadpool cannot be starved.
- **Ground-truth corrected the plan (verified from source before coding):** real NCalc version is **6.1.1** (props declared it correctly; the local `project.assets.json` was stale from before the 2026-07-21 bump — force-restore resolved 6.1.1; "assets says 5.12.0" was a stale artifact, not a downgrade, nearly a false CVE alarm). NCalc 6.1.1 exposes **no** native step/iteration/recursion/timeout guard (the plan's "prefer NCalc native limit" branch was a seam that does not exist) and has **zero user-reachable loop/recursion built-in** — the heaviest expression fitting the 500-char cap (a deep `Pow` chain) evals in ~20ms and overflows to ∞, not a hang. The classic formula-DoS surface is therefore already closed by NCalc 6.1.1 + the length cap, so the semaphore and the fail-closed built-in allowlist are **forward-insurance**, and the concurrency oracle test is scoped to concurrency-safety, not a starvation simulation that cannot exist.
- **Signature migrated to async** (`Evaluate`→`EvaluateAsync`+`CancellationToken`) across 4 verified call sites (`FormDataPreprocessor` + `SubmitForm`/`SubmitPublicForm` handlers, all already async); interface is Forms-internal, 0 FE-impact (formula is server-computed).
- **Code review caught one CONFIRMED regression:** the first cut bound params via `Parameters[key]=val`, which sets only keys **present** in the submission — but the FE (`form-submission-helpers.ts:30,33`) omits a field key when it is hidden-by-visibility or an untouched optional, so a formula over such a field silently returned null instead of computing with 0. Fixed by restoring the `EvaluateParameter` 0-substitution event (preserves the lenient "missing field ⇒ 0" contract) plus a `ReferencesAbsentField_SubstitutesZero` regression test. Renaming `PreprocessData`→`PreprocessDataAsync` also touched 11 test call sites invisible to a `src/`-only grep.

## Fix — OIDC SPA Redirect URIs Bound from Config (OIDC-SPA-CLIENT-REDIRECT-URIS-HARDCODED) (2026-07-28, auth)

**Type:** fix (launch blocker `[blocks-v1.0]`) · plan `260728-1331-oidc-spa-redirect-uris-from-config`, 3 phases · code review **3 rounds** (BLOCKED → DONE_WITH_CONCERNS → DONE) · AuthServer build `-warnaserror` 0W/0E · AuthServer unit 40/40 · Startup smoke 3/3 on a clean bin · architecture 203/203. +203/-115 LOC.

- **The defect:** `OpenIddictDataSeeder.SeedApplicationsAsync` hardcoded the `aqtcorefw-spa-dev` client's redirect and post-logout URIs to `localhost:{3000,4200,5173}`. The seeder runs in **every** environment (`Program.cs:487` has no env gate, unlike dev-user seeding at `:490`), so any non-localhost deploy — the kind cluster at `app.aqt.localtest.me`, or production — registered a client that fails every authorize round-trip with `redirect_uri` mismatch. It survived P1/P2 because those smokes only check the discovery document.
- **The fix:** URIs bind from `Auth:SpaClient:{RedirectUris,PostLogoutRedirectUris}` through a new `SpaClientRedirectUris.Resolve`. Development falls back to the exact previous localhost list, so the dev loop, `.http` files, Playwright e2e and Swagger keep working with zero config. Outside Development a missing or blank value **throws at startup**, naming the config key — same posture as `Program.LoadRequiredCertificate`. `values-local.yaml` supplies the `*.localtest.me` set via indexed env keys; the base chart deliberately supplies none, so the first prod deploy fails loudly at boot rather than quietly at login.
- **Blank values are filtered before the configured-vs-absent decision**, so a committed-but-empty config value fails exactly like an absent one. This is the `""`-defeats-`??` trap the repo has hit repeatedly; two tests pin it.
- **Resolve and validate now happen before `DeleteAsync`.** The client is delete-and-recreated on every boot, so a configuration error discovered mid-way would previously have left a deployment with no SPA client and no way to log in.
- **A refuted assumption, caught by review, worth recording.** Mid-slice the post-logout list was reduced 8→4 entries on the belief that OpenIddict normalizes these URIs. It does not: `new Uri("http://h:p")` equals `new Uri("http://h:p/")`, so the descriptor's `ISet<Uri>` keeps only the **first-inserted** spelling; OpenIddict persists that instance's `Uri.OriginalString` without normalizing, then matches logout requests with `StringComparison.Ordinal` (its relaxed URI-parsing branch is gated on native clients — this one is Public). The SPA sends `window.location.origin`, always slashless. Storing the slash form would have returned **400 invalid_request on every logout** in dev, kind and tunnel demos. Both spellings restored, slashless first, in all four write paths; pinned by a mutation-verified test.
- **A false green closed alongside it.** The integration test appeared to cover the hardcoded fallback but was reading an `Auth:SpaClient` section that the tunnel script had left in the committed dev config — it stayed green straight through the defect above. That section is out of the committed config (the C# fallback is the single source of truth for zero-config dev) and `--restore` now **deletes** the key rather than rewriting it, so a developer cannot reintroduce it by finishing a tunnel demo. Verified both ways: with the section present the slash-first mutation left the test green; with it absent the same mutation turns it red.
- **`scripts/3_setup-tunnel-urls.py` no longer regex-rewrites C# source** — it writes the same config keys the deployment path uses. It also now emits the `localhost:3000`/`4200`/`127.0.0.1` origins, because configured values *replace* the fallback rather than merging, and `infra/docker/smoke-test.sh` hardcodes `localhost:3000/callback`.
- **Not yet verified:** no real browser login has been performed against the kind cluster. This slice removes the code blocker; the round-trip itself, and logout in particular (the ordinal-match path has no integration coverage), are tracked by `OIDC-BROWSER-LOGIN-ROUNDTRIP-VERIFY-ON-KIND`. Prod origins still need an overlay — `AUTHSERVER-PROD-VALUES-SPA-REDIRECT-URIS`.

## Fix — Local k8s Data Tier Persisted; Soak Post-Mortem (VAULT-DEVMODE-INMEMORY-KILLS-SOAK) (2026-07-25, infra) — `d04d6b842`

**Type:** fix (local rehearsal infra) · code-review 1 Critical + 1 High + 4 Medium → C1/H1/H2/M1/M3/M4 fixed in-slice · verified empirically on the live kind cluster (no unit tests — infra manifests + shell). +413/-22 LOC.

- **Soak outcome, stated honestly: the ≥24h criterion was NOT met.** The run started 2026-07-23T12:59Z produced **~2.5h of valid clean data** (restarts=0 through 14:50Z, one CSV sample at 13:11Z all-green), then the API and AuthServer CrashLooped for ~36h to **146 restarts**. Evidence from Prometheus retention (`kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total`): `restarts=15` by 07-24 01:50Z, climbing ~11.5/h at the 5-min backoff cap. One clean sample is not a 24h pass — plan `260723-1258-*` P3 is recorded COMPLETE-PARTIAL, not closed.
- **Root cause was the environment, not the application.** Vault ran dev-mode (in-memory storage) and SQL Server on `emptyDir`. A host sleep/resume restarted both pods, wiping every secret and the entire schema; `ProductionSecretValidator` then **correctly** refused to boot (`Production secret missing or contains DEV marker: Encryption:FieldKey`; the accompanying `[Vault] Could not load secrets from Vault: {"errors":[]}` is a 404 on an empty store, not a credential failure). The dev-mode limitation was already written in the plan's §Secrets hygiene — what was never computed was its effect on a multi-day soak.
- **Fix:** Vault moved to `storage "file"` on a 1Gi PVC with an `unseal` sidecar (`infra/k8s-local/vault-unseal.sh`) that initializes on first boot and re-unseals after every restart; SQL Server moved to a 10Gi PVC. Both use `strategy: Recreate` so two writers never share one volume.
- **New hazard created by the fix, and its guard:** because the data tier now survives, `scripts/k8s-local-reseed.sh` is no longer freely re-runnable — step 5b mints NEW random encryption keys, which against a surviving database would orphan the key its existing rows were encrypted under. The script now refuses to run while the data PVCs exist and requires `RESET_DATA=1` to wipe data and keys together. That path `helm uninstall`s the releases rather than deleting their objects, since helm does not reliably recreate resources removed behind its back.
- **Three behaviours established by probing rather than assumption, each now commented beside the code that depends on it:** (1) the `hashicorp/vault` image ships **no curl**, so the unseal key lives on the vault PVC beside the data it unlocks instead of in a Kubernetes Secret (key and data can never drift apart); (2) `vault ... -format=json` is **pretty-printed**, so line-based patterns matching `"field":value` silently never fire — this bit in **3 separate places** in one slice, and in the init path it produced an empty unseal key *after* `operator init` had irreversibly run, leaving an initialized-but-unopenable vault; (3) `vault status` **exits 2 when sealed** — a status code, not a failure, so `|| fallback` discards valid JSON.
- **Review C1 (Critical, fixed in-slice):** `initialize || log ...` disables `set -e` for the **entire body** of the callee, so `store_key`'s `return 1` was discarded and execution continued into `operator unseal` / `token create` / `secrets enable` — reproducing exactly the unrecoverable state the function exists to prevent. Every must-not-skip step after the irreversible `operator init` is now checked explicitly. **H1:** `exit 1` inside the reconciler killed the sidecar and scrolled the cause out of the logs (`return 1` now). **M4:** a 403 from `vault secrets list` was indistinguishable from "kv-v2 not enabled"; output and exit code are now checked separately.
- **Verified from zero on the live cluster:** reseed → 3 charts deployed → smoke ALL GREEN; then deleted the vault and sqlserver pods → vault auto-unsealed from the stored key, all app pods stayed at **0 restarts**, **200 tables survived** without re-running migrations, smoke ALL GREEN again — precisely the scenario that killed the soak.
- **Local-only posture, explicitly not production:** 1 key share / threshold 1, unseal key unencrypted beside its data so a local reset discards both. Production still needs a real unseal ceremony with split key custody, HA, k8s auth and audit devices. Stale claims corrected in `infra/k8s-local/README.md` and `docs/deployment-guide.md` §122-126.
- **Residual, deliberately out of scope:** `audit-read-isolation` reports Degraded after a from-zero reset because the NonAudit SQL login is a manual DBA step outside the reseed script (row `P1-STABLE-AUDIT-ISO-OPS-ACTIVATE` already tracks it). The ≥24h soak criterion itself is carried to a staging gate (`SOAK-24H-REQUIRES-STAGING-NOT-LAPTOP`) rather than waived — a laptop that sleeps cannot host a trustworthy 24h soak.

## Fix — Alert Test Button: One Rule, Real Outcome (ALERTING-TESTRULE-REPORTS-202-ON-FAILED-DELIVERY) (2026-07-21, observability + admin API)

**Type:** fix (3 defects, row named only 1) · plan `plans/260721-1647-alerting-testrule-single-rule-outcome/` · branch `fix/alerting-testrule-single-rule-outcome` · code-review Critical (1, fixed in-slice) · `AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure.Extensions.Tests` 216 passed/1 pre-existing skip (alerting subset 34/34, up from 25) · Architecture 185/185. Closure criterion: **local-verify**, not CI-observed (GitHub Actions disabled by user choice).

- **Row understated the defect.** Filed 2026-07-17 against `POST /admin/alerts/{id}/test` returning 202 on a failed delivery. Reading `AlertingAdminController.cs` against `AlertEvaluationJob.cs` found three defects, the swallowed outcome being the smallest: (1) the endpoint called `ExecuteAsync()`, which evaluates every **enabled** rule — testing rule X could fire rule Y's real notification and record a breach on Y; (2) a **disabled** rule — the state a freshly seeded rule starts in — was never evaluated, yet the endpoint still answered 202; (3) the per-rule catch in `ExecuteAsync` swallowed dispatch failures, so no outcome could reach the controller. The row's proposed fix (return per-rule outcomes from `ExecuteAsync`) addressed only #3.
- **Shipped:** new `AlertEvaluationJob.TestRuleAsync(rule, ct)` — evaluates exactly the requested rule, enabled or not, really dispatches on breach, and writes **no state** (no `RecordBreach`, no `ConsecutiveBreaches`/`LastTriggeredAt` change, no audit entry, no `SaveChanges`). Returns `AlertRuleTestOutcome` (`Evaluated`, `MetricValue`, `Breached`, `Dispatch`) wrapping a new `AlertDispatchOutcome` (`Channel`, `Delivered`, `Detail`). `ExecuteAsync`'s signature, scheduled behaviour, and per-rule exception handling are untouched — a shared `DispatchAsync`/`SendEmailAsync`/`PostWebhookAsync` internal path now takes a `source` parameter instead of being duplicated.
- **Controller:** `TestRule` now returns `200 OK` with the outcome body (was `202 Accepted`, no body), `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(ApiResponse<AlertRuleTestOutcome>), 200)]` — the untyped 202 attribute would have regenerated the Orval FE client as `void`, hiding the new body from the FE and reintroducing the defect client-side.
- **Code-review Critical, fixed in-slice — the test path shared the scheduled evaluator's metric counters.** Against the alert thresholds shipped this same morning (see the self-monitoring entry below), three admin test presses would trip `AqtCoreFWAlertEvaluationFailing` (`> 5` over 5m; a failing press records 2 increments) and **one** press against a broken EMAIL rule would trip `AqtCoreFWAlertNotificationFailing` (`> 0`) — the single most likely use of this button — paging ops about a healthy evaluator. Fixed with a `source` tag (`scheduled` / `test`) on all 7 `AlertingMetrics` increment sites in `AlertEvaluationJob`; both Prometheus alert expressions in `infra/helm/aqtcorefw/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` and the seeded self-monitor rule's `MetricName` in `AlertRuleDevSeeder.cs` narrowed to `source="scheduled"`. `infra/prometheus/alert-rules-test.yml` carried no `source` label on its fixture series and would have silently stopped matching — updated, plus 2 new cases proving a burst of `source="test"` series stays silent. **`promtool` is not installed locally — those fixtures were updated for consistency but not executed; caveat recorded, not hidden.**
- **Mutation-proved twice:** injecting `await ExecuteAsync(ct)` at the top of `TestRuleAsync` turned 3 of 6 new facts red (`DoesNotEvaluateOtherRules`, `WritesNoState`, `ReallyDispatches`); flipping `TestSource` to `"scheduled"` turned both new source-tag facts red. Green on revert each time.
- **FE consumer: none (verified).** `web/src/api/generated/alerting-admin/alerting-admin.ts` has an Orval-generated `usePostApiV1AdminAlertsIdTest` hook typed against the old `void`/202 shape, with **zero** callers outside the generated file anywhere in `web/src`. The 202→200 change breaks no live caller; the defect was latent. Regenerating the Orval client is left as a mechanical step for whoever builds the admin screen — deliberately not done blind here.
- **Not applied (reviewer-raised, non-blocking):** truncating `Detail`'s exception text (reachable only by an MFA'd SystemAdmin who can already read the rule and its target; `ex.Message` not `ToString()`, no stack trace) and passing `rule` by value to make state-freedom structural (the `WritesNoState` test is the regression net for that).
- **Contract:** `ExecuteAsync` signature unchanged; new public `TestRuleAsync` method + 2 new public records (`AlertRuleTestOutcome`, `AlertDispatchOutcome`) on `AlertEvaluationJob`. `POST /admin/alerts/{id}/test` response shape changed (202→200, no body → typed body) — no live FE caller.

Sibling of the EMAIL half fixed 2026-07-17 (`NOTIFICATIONS-RECIPIENT-IS-GUID-NOT-ADDRESS`), filed as follow-up `NOTIFICATIONS-SMS-RECIPIENT-IS-GUID-NOT-PHONE` at the time.

Rejected — `GetUserInfoByIdsAsync` feeds 25 display-name enrichment call sites incl. SignalR broadcasts, and the phone number is Confidential PII (QĐ 742 §66); widening a broadly-consumed DTO would hand it to every caller regardless of need. Instead added a PII-scoped contract method, `IIdentityModuleClient.GetUserPhoneNumbersByIdsAsync(userIds, tenantId, ct)` — `UserInfoDto` unchanged, zero existing consumers edited. `tenantId` is REQUIRED here (unlike the optional filter on sibling lookups): `identity.AspNetUsers` carries no RLS policy (absent from `RlsPolicyPresenceTests`), so this SQL predicate is the only tenant isolation on the read.

The line predates this work (`a7919abf7`) and was harmless while the value was a Guid; this fix turned it into a plaintext Confidential-PII log sink. Masked to last-4 digits at the call site (`WebhookSmsProvider.MaskPhoneNumber`) in both log lines.

## Fix/Feature — Alerting Self-Monitoring: Revived Dead Prometheus Metrics + Failure Counters + Self-Monitor Rule (ALERTING-LOGCRITICAL-HAS-NO-ALERT) (2026-07-21, observability)

**Type:** fix (Prometheus exporter, pre-existing blocking defect) + feat (self-monitoring counters + rule) · plan `plans/260721-1130-alerting-selfmonitor-metrics-prometheus-exporter/` · PR #126, merge `822f15027` · code-review DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (0 Critical/0 High, 3 Medium applied in-slice) · `AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure.Extensions.Tests` 207 passed/1 pre-existing skip · alerting subset 25/25 stable across 3 consecutive runs · Architecture 185/185 · `AqtCoreFW.Notifications.Infrastructure` 16/16 · full solution build 0 errors, no new warnings in touched files. Closure criterion: **local-verify**, not CI-observed (GitHub Actions disabled by user choice).

- **Row's own prescribed fix was infeasible:** the row asked for "an ops-side alert on the job's `LogCritical`, not more guard code." Scouting proved that cannot exist here — log sinks are Console + File only (`SerilogConfiguration.cs:27-33`), no aggregator attached; and a repo-wide search for `*alert*`/`*alertmanager*`/`prometheus*.yml` under `infra/` returned zero (`infra/prometheus/recording-rules.yml` holds recording rules only). Nothing to alert on, nowhere to put a rule. Pivoted, user-approved, to metric counters + a self-monitor `AlertRule`.
- **Pre-existing blocking defect found while scoping, bigger than the row itself:** application `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` meters were registered via `.AddMeter(...)` in `OpenTelemetryConfiguration.cs` but exported through OTLP only, while `/metrics` is served by prometheus-net, which cannot read those meters. Every module counter shipped since 2026-07-04 — `audit_ingestion_lost_total`, `signing_provider_allowlist_denied_total`, and the rest — was invisible to anything querying Prometheus, including `AlertEvaluationJob` itself, which alerts BY querying Prometheus over HTTP. A rule seeded 2026-07-04 against `signing_provider_allowlist_denied_total` would have been silent forever had ops enabled it. Fixed first, in its own commit (`0bb63099b`), because it has standalone value: it revived 8 already-shipped-but-dead counters.
- **Shipped in `0bb63099b`:** package `OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Prometheus.AspNetCore` 1.15.3-beta.1 (pinned in `src/Directory.Packages.props` — this package has never shipped a stable release; the -beta matching the repo's pinned OTel 1.15.3 line was chosen, alongside the existing prerelease precedent `OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EntityFrameworkCore` 1.15.1-beta.1), `.AddPrometheusExporter()` on the metrics pipeline, and a new `/metrics-otel` endpoint via `MapOtelMetricsEndpoint`. Route deliberately separate from `/metrics`: both are terminal handlers writing a complete Prometheus exposition body, so sharing a path would let whichever registered first answer every scrape while the other's series vanish silently. `infra/helm/aqtcorefw/templates/servicemonitor.yaml` gained a second endpoint block scraping both. Three telemetry classes (`AuditMetrics.cs`, `SigningMetrics.cs`, `CollaborationMetrics.cs`) carried XML docs asserting "the Prometheus exporter appends the conventional `_total` suffix" — a claim about a pipeline that never existed; corrected.
- **Metric names were observed, not derived:** a throwaway host using the identical package pair was run and scraped live. Annotation-only UCUM units (`{event}`, `{denial}`, `{failure}`) contribute NO suffix — counters are dots→underscores plus `_total` — so the 2026-07-04 seed string needed no change. A REAL unit DOES suffix: `workflow.execute_transition.duration_ms` with unit `ms` exports as `workflow_execute_transition_duration_ms_milliseconds`. Any future rule over a histogram must use the suffixed name.
- **Shipped in `c6b09a283`:** new `AlertingMetrics` (`src/shared/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure/Alerting/AlertingMetrics.cs`) — two counters, `alerting_notification_failed_total{channel,reason}` (channel = `email`|`webhook`; reason = `unconfigured`|`delivery_failed`|`http_error`) and `alerting_evaluation_failed_total{reason}` (reason = `query_failed`|`no_data`|`rule_error`), both closed literal tag sets. Deliberately NOT tagged with `AlertRule.Name` (operator-supplied, unbounded cardinality) or `NotifyTarget` (an email address — PII in a scraped Prometheus label). Wired into all 6 failure branches of `AlertEvaluationJob` (email unconfigured / email delivery-failed / webhook http-error / webhook delivery-failed / query-failed / no-data / rule-error) with no control-flow change — counting only. Plus a self-monitor rule appended to `AlertRuleDevSeeder.DevRules`, seeded DISABLED on the `Log` channel (a rule watching notification failures must not report through a channel it monitors). Intended double-count documented, not a defect: `QueryPrometheusAsync` returns null for both a throw and a genuinely empty result and the caller cannot distinguish, so a thrown query increments both `query_failed` and `no_data`.
- **End-to-end verification (live process):** with the seeded rule enabled and no Prometheus in dev, `/metrics-otel` returned `alerting_evaluation_failed_total{reason="query_failed"} 1` and `{reason="no_data"} 1`.
- **Code review on PR #126:** DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, 0 Critical/0 High. Disproved the false-green risk empirically by mutating production code twice (both caught by the new tests, file restored byte-exact). Three Mediums applied: (a) `docs/dependency-map.md` DID need an entry — the "Infrastructure-internal" assumption was wrong, `SigningMetrics` already documents that exact shape at line 654; (b) `/metrics-otel` also serves ASP.NET Core/HttpClient/runtime instrumentation, so the doc was corrected to say what is actually exported; (c) **self-monitor threshold `GT 10` → `GT 5`** — a continuously failing rule yields ~10 per 5-minute window (2 increments × 5 runs) and `GT 10` is false at exactly 10, so with a single enabled rule it would never have fired; now pinned by a test carrying the arithmetic.
- **Contract:** none — additive counters + additive scrape endpoint. `AddGovHealthChecks`/`AlertingRegistration` signatures unchanged.
- **Follow-up filed:** `PROMETHEUS-DEADMAN-SWITCH-MISSING` (see below).

### Follow-on, same session — `PROMETHEUS-DEADMAN-SWITCH-MISSING`: partially shipped, deliberately left OPEN

Filed from the PR #126 review, then partially shipped in the same session.

- **Commit `38e6b543d`:** new `infra/helm/aqtcorefw/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` — a Prometheus Operator `PrometheusRule` with 4 alerts: `AqtCoreFWDown` (`up{service="<fullname>"} == 0`, `for: 2m`), `AqtCoreFWWatchdog` (`vector(1)`, always-firing heartbeat, `severity: none`), `AqtCoreFWAlertEvaluationFailing`, `AqtCoreFWAlertNotificationFailing`. Gated behind `metrics.prometheusRule.enabled`. Rationale: the in-app evaluator reaches its own metrics BY querying Prometheus, so it structurally cannot report a Prometheus outage — every rule's query fails at once, all read as non-breaching, alerting goes silent with no breach. These rules live outside that query path. Plus `infra/prometheus/alert-rules-test.yml`, promtool behaviour tests covering firing AND non-firing cases, run against a genuine `helm template` render. The `up{service=...}` selector uses the `service` label (the Operator derives it from the Service name) rather than `job`, whose naming has varied across operator versions.
- **Commit `498f954bf`:** **`metrics.prometheusRule.enabled` set to `false` in EVERY values file, production included** (it was briefly `true` in prod). Reason: the user confirmed CoreBase has **never been deployed to production**. `values-prod.yaml` setting `serviceMonitor.enabled: true` with `release: prometheus` had been read as evidence that a kube-prometheus-stack Operator exists — it is not evidence, it is an intention no deploy has ever exercised, and that label is the stack's default only when installed under the Helm release name `prometheus`. Shipping the rules enabled would assert alert coverage never observed to work. `docs/deployment-guide.md` §9 was rewritten from a post-deploy check into an ordered 5-step enable procedure for the first real deploy: read the cluster's real `ruleSelector` (a DIFFERENT Operator field from `serviceMonitorSelector`, so a working ServiceMonitor does not prove rules load); set labels to match; flip the flag; confirm via the Prometheus API that rules actually LOADED (a mismatch leaves the object present and silently ignored); route the watchdog to an external heartbeat receiver or it fires into a void; tune thresholds on real traffic.

## Fix/Ops — Migration Pre-Deploy Dry-Run: Hangfire Boot-Lock Retry + Preflight Probe (P1-STABLE-MIGRATION-PREDEPLOY-DRYRUN) (2026-07-21, ops resilience)

**Type:** fix (Hangfire boot resilience) + ops (SQL preflight script) · plan `plans/260721-0900-p1-stable-migration-predeploy-dryrun/plan.md` · branch `feat/p1-stable-migration-predeploy-dryrun` · code-review DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (0 Critical/0 High; 1 Medium comment-sharpen fixed in-slice, 2 Low benign) · build `src/AqtCoreFW.slnx` 0W/0E · new unit tests 8/8. Closure criterion: **local-verify**, not CI-observed (GitHub Actions disabled by user choice).

Row sourced from `plans/reports/audit-260716-1805-stable-monolith-p1-operational-readiness-report.md` §1 #6 (Hangfire boot-lock) + #3 (migration dry-run). Two independent concerns, one row, scope user-locked to these two.

- **Concern A — Hangfire boot distributed-lock timeout unhandled:** recurring-job registration at API boot drives Hangfire's static `RecurringJob` facade, which acquires a SQL distributed lock; on a contended/slow-SQL boot, a transient lock timeout previously hard-failed the entire host (K8s restart-storm risk on sustained contention). New `RecurringJobRegistrationRetry` (`src/shared/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure/BackgroundJobs/RecurringJobRegistrationRetry.cs`) — `IsTransientLockFailure` classifies `DistributedLockTimeoutException` + `SqlException` error 1222/-2 (type+error-number match, not message text); `RunWithRetry` retries 3 attempts with 2s/4s/6s backoff, then **fails soft**: logs Critical and lets boot continue. Fail-soft only skips *re-registration* — already-persisted schedules keep firing (incl. compliance jobs: audit-log purge / RTBF SLA / alert eval) regardless of whether this boot re-registered them. Non-transient exceptions (e.g. a wiring bug) rethrow immediately, unswallowed.
  `src/host/AqtCoreFW.Api/Program.cs` (~L437-505) wraps the existing 12 recurring-job registration calls in `RunWithRetry` — pure lambda-wrap, calls unchanged verbatim, zero behavior change on the happy path.
- **Concern B — no pre-deploy migration dry-run vs prod-like data:** the `UX_FormTemplate_PublicCode` filtered-unique-index migration (`20260709082745_AddFormTemplatePublicCodeUniqueIndex`) carries a fail-loud `THROW 50000` guard that aborts `MigrateAsync` (and thus host boot) when dirty cross-tenant-duplicate data is present — previously discoverable only mid-deploy (real prior incident: `FORMS-DEV-DB-DUPLICATE-PUBLIC-CODE-MIGRATION-BLOCK`, resolved `99fc5cb0`). ## Fix — Restore-Drill Temp File Cleanup (BACKUP-RESTORE-DRILL-TEMP-CLEANUP) (2026-07-21, low-tier fix)

**Type:** fix (resource leak) · branch `fix/backup-restore-drill-temp-cleanup` · code-review DONE (0 Critical/0 High) · shared infra build 0W/0E · 4/4 new unit tests · 6/6 `BackupRetentionPruner` tests unchanged. FU of `P1-STABLE-BACKUP-AUTOMATION`, filed 2026-07-16 from code-review.

- **Bug closed:** `DatabaseBackupService.ExecuteRestoreDrillAsync` left `_drill_*.bak`/`.mdf`/`.ldf` temp files uncleaned in `Backup:Directory` — the drill `.bak` record is excluded from retention prune (`BackupRetentionPruner.SelectExpired` selects only `Type == "Backup"/"ScheduledBackup"`) and the `.mdf`/`.ldf` files never get a DB record at all, so the `/backups` volume accumulated drill artifacts indefinitely.
- **Fix:** new `DrillTempFileCleanup.TryDelete(paths, logger)` (`src/shared/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure/Backup/DrillTempFileCleanup.cs`) — best-effort delete, swallows `IOException`/`UnauthorizedAccessException`/`PathTooLongException` with a `LogWarning`, never throws (mirrors the `BackupRetentionPruner` precedent). `ExecuteRestoreDrillAsync` hoists its 3 temp-path locals above the `try` and calls the helper on all three from a new `finally`, so cleanup runs on both success and mid-drill failure; `MarkCompleted` still captures the file size inside the `try`, before the file is deleted.
- **Design (user-approved):** delete all 3 files including the drill `.bak` — a drill artifact is ephemeral restore-verification, never a recovery source.
- **Known-limit accepted (user 2026-07-21):** if the drill fails between restore and temp-DB drop, SQL Server still holds OS locks on `.mdf`/`.ldf`, so the delete is swallowed and the files persist until a later run — a rare, logged, bounded leak on that one failure branch only (success path and every `.bak` always clean). Documented inline in the helper's XML doc; user declined an in-slice fix (would need `DROP DATABASE` in its own nested `finally`) and did not want a separate follow-up row.
- **Contract:** none — additive helper, no DI registration, `finally`-only change to the caller. `docs/dependency-map.md` not updated (same-assembly internal helper, single caller, no cross-module edge).

## Fix — Notification Recipient Resolution: Email Half (NOTIFICATIONS-RECIPIENT-IS-GUID-NOT-ADDRESS, EMAIL half) (2026-07-17, bug fix + security)

**Type:** fix (bug + security) · plan `plans/260717-2015-notifications-recipient-guid-not-address/plan.md` · branch `fix/notifications-resolve-recipient-email` · code-review REQUEST_CHANGES (2 High) → both fixed in-slice → APPROVE_WITH_NITS · build `src/AqtCoreFW.slnx` 0W/0E · arch **185/185** (was 180, +5) · `AqtCoreFW.Notifications.Application` 35/35 (was 30) · `AqtCoreFW.Workflow.Application` 642/642 · `AqtCoreFW.Forms.Application` 344/344. Closure criterion: **local-verify**, not CI-observed (GitHub Actions disabled by user choice).

- **Bug closed:** `SendNotificationCommandHandler.cs:67` passed `request.RecipientUserId.ToString()` (a Guid) directly as the SMTP `to` address; `MailKitEmailSender.cs:21`'s `MailboxAddress.Parse` threw on every Email notification through `INotificationModuleClient` and the direct `POST /api/v1/notifications` path. Fixed: the handler now resolves the recipient's actual email via `IIdentityModuleClient.GetUserInfoByIdsAsync([RecipientUserId], request.TenantId, ct)` **inside the email branch only** — the `"inapp"` path (every Forms notification today) gains zero identity round-trips. Not found / null `Email` → `Result.Fail` naming the failure + `MarkAsFailed` on the persisted row (no throw, no infinite Hangfire/MediatR retry of an unresolvable user).
- **New cross-module edge:** `Notifications.Application` gains a `ProjectReference` to `AqtCoreFW.Identity.Contracts` (zero-ProjectReference leaf, no cycle — same leaf-edge precedent as `Notification.Contracts`/`OrgUnit.Contracts`). Keeps the Email AES-GCM decryption and tenant filter in the one place (`InProcessIdentityModuleClient`) that already implements them correctly, rather than hand-rolling a Dapper read that would have mailed ciphertext.
- **SECURITY — code-review caught a dormant hole the fix armed (High #1):** `NotificationsController.Send` bound `TenantId` from the **request body**, while every sibling action on the same controller uses `ResolveTenantId()`. Before this slice that binding was inert — the handler mailed a Guid, MailKit threw, nothing was delivered. **After** the email fix landed, the handler resolves a real decrypted mailbox from that client-supplied tenant, turning any holder of the notification-send permission into a cross-tenant phishing primitive with a user-existence oracle (200 vs 422 response). **This slice did not introduce the tenant-binding gap — it activated it, and fixed it in the same commit set**, before merge: the controller now binds `ResolveTenantId()`, matching all sibling actions. Net effect: cross-tenant sends now require SystemAdmin (via the existing `X-Tenant-Id` header path), same as every other action on the controller — no legitimate capability lost.
- **High #2 — silent-failure gap:** the slice's own risk assessment assumed "callers handle `Result.Fail`"; code-review found they do not — `InProcessNotificationModuleClient.cs:25` discards the Result (fire-and-forget), and both live event-handler callers ignore it too. Unfixed, the recipient-resolution failure path would have traded a loud `FormatException` in the logs for total silence. Fixed: the failure branch now `LogWarning`s (naming the notification + reason) before marking the row Failed.
- **SMS is still broken — NOT fixed this slice.** `SendNotificationCommandHandler.cs:69` has the identical Guid-as-target defect on the SMS path (`WebhookSmsProvider`). Cannot be fixed the same way: `UserInfoDto` has no `PhoneNumber` field. Follow-up filed: `NOTIFICATIONS-SMS-RECIPIENT-IS-GUID-NOT-PHONE`. The pre-existing test pinning the SMS defect is kept and annotated, not deleted or silently fixed.
- **Tests:** email test rewritten to assert the resolved address (was asserting the Guid — the bug itself); new not-found + null-email failure cases; new inapp test asserts **zero** `IIdentityModuleClient` calls; SMS test kept, annotated as pinning a known defect. New `NotificationSendTenantBindingTests` (5 tests, `tests/architecture/AqtCoreFW.Architecture.Tests/`) pin the `ResolveTenantId()` fix — placed in `Architecture.Tests` because the repo has no `*.Presentation.Tests` project (that project already references `Notifications.Presentation`); flagged as a placement question, not resolved (follow-up `NOTIFICATIONS-PRESENTATION-TESTS-PLACEMENT`).
- **Non-vacuity proven by mutation** (each reverted): restoring `RecipientUserId.ToString()` → email test fails · hoisting the lookup above the channel switch → inapp + tenant tests fail · re-trusting the body tenant → 4 of 5 tenant-binding tests fail · removing `MarkAsFailed()` on the early-return path → that test fails (reviewer-found).
- **Contract:** `IIdentityModuleClient`, `UserInfoDto`, `IEmailSender`, `ISmsProvider`, `SendNotificationCommand`, `INotificationModuleClient` all unchanged — new consumption only, no signature change.
- **Follow-ups filed:** `NOTIFICATIONS-SMS-RECIPIENT-IS-GUID-NOT-PHONE` (🟠 T2 — needs `PhoneNumber` added to `UserInfoDto` + the Identity Dapper projection extended; check whether `ApplicationUser.PhoneNumber` is encrypted at rest like `Email` before projecting it) · `NOTIFICATIONS-PRESENTATION-TESTS-PLACEMENT` (🔵 T4 — repo-wide test-project-layout question, not urgent).

## Feature — RabbitMQ Readiness Probe, Transport-Gated (P1-STABLE-RABBITMQ-HEALTHCHECK) (2026-07-17, observability)

**Type:** feat · commit `1613bdd1` on `main` (pushed) · code-review REQUEST_CHANGES → APPROVE_WITH_NITS after fixes · full solution build 0W/0E · `AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure.Extensions.Tests` 183/183 (+4 over the 179 baseline), 1 pre-existing skip.

- **Gap closed:** `/health/ready` covered SqlServer/Redis/Vault/audit-isolation (+ optional qdrant/ollama) but not the message broker, so readiness stayed green until a send actually failed. New probe in `AddGovHealthChecks` (`src/shared/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure/HealthChecks/HealthCheckConfiguration.cs`) via new dependency `AspNetCore.HealthChecks.Rabbitmq` 9.0.0 (version-aligned with the SqlServer/Redis siblings), tagged `["messaging","ready"]`.
- **Transport-gated** (user decision): registers ONLY when `Bus:Transport == "RabbitMQ"`. The bus defaults to InMemory (`MessagingRegistration.cs:47`), so an unconditional probe would report Degraded about a broker the system never connects to — trading a false-green for a false-red. Mirrors the existing `AI:Ollama:Enabled` gate for the qdrant/ollama probes in the same method.
- **`Degraded`, not `Unhealthy`** (matching Redis, not SqlServer): the outbox + 5s/30s/5m retry absorb a transient outage and most HTTP traffic never touches the broker, so an outage must not pull the pod out of rotation.
- **Critical caught in code-review — connection leak:** the first cut passed `async _ => await factory.CreateConnectionAsync()` to `AddRabbitMQ` under a code comment asserting the package caches the resolved connection. The comment was an unverified assumption; the package's own shipped XML doc says the opposite ("factory will be called each time the healthcheck route is requested") and the async overload never disposes the result → ~8,640 leaked connections/pod/day at the Helm `periodSeconds: 10` cadence, manifesting only on the HEALTHY path in prod-only config (the gate strips the probe in dev/CI). Fixed with new `ProbeConnectionSource` (`src/shared/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure/HealthChecks/ProbeConnectionSource.cs`) — one cached `IConnection`, `SemaphoreSlim`-gated double-checked `IsOpen` re-check, dispose-before-reconnect. Takes `Func<Task<IConnection>>` rather than the unmockable concrete `ConnectionFactory`; that seam is what makes the cache testable.
- **Second-order fix (same class):** the first timeout fix passed `timeout: 3s` to `AddRabbitMQ` assuming it bounded the probe — it does not; the framework's linked-token/`CancelAfter` reaches `CreateChannelAsync` only, never the connection factory. A black-holing broker would hold the connect for `RequestedConnectionTimeout` (empirically 30s default, measured against RabbitMQ.Client 7.0.0). Fixed by also setting `RequestedConnectionTimeout = 3s` on the factory.
- **Tests:** 9 new in `tests/unit/AqtCoreFW.Infrastructure.Extensions.Tests/HealthChecks/` — `RabbitMqHealthCheckRegistrationTests` (5 cases) drives the REAL `AddGovHealthChecks` and reads back `HealthCheckServiceOptions.Registrations`; `ProbeConnectionSourceTests` (4 facts) pins the cache. Mutation-proven twice: inverting the gate → 3 RED; disabling both cache branches → the 2 cache tests RED. Both restored.
- **Dependency note:** `RabbitMQ.Client` resolves to 7.0.0 — the same version MassTransit.RabbitMQ 8.3.6 depends on, so no downgrade/conflict.
- **Contract:** none — `AddGovHealthChecks(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration)` unchanged; probe is additive and gated off by default.
- **HONESTY — probe is dormant:** every config in the repo sets `Bus:Transport=InMemory`, so nothing exercises it today, and the broker-down→Degraded criterion has NO automated test (package behavior, needs a live broker; deliberately not mocked into a false-green). Follow-up `RABBITMQ-HEALTHCHECK-LIVE-BROKER-VERIFY` filed to verify both at RabbitMQ cutover.

## Fix — Smoke-Gate Hardening: 3 Bugs Behind One Symptom, Incl. a Real AuthServer Prod DI Regression (SMOKE-FIXTURE-ENV-VAR-RACE-HARDENING) (2026-07-17, test-infra + prod-fix)

**Type:** fix (2 test-infra bugs + 1 real prod bug) · commits `88b28227` / `90867b13` / `da8b3ea5`, merged to `main` 2026-07-17 via PR #121 (`fc097de5`) · follow-on investigation from the 2026-07-16 CI smoke-gate ship below · code-review APPROVE, 0 Critical/0 High · smoke suite 11/11 GREEN, verified 3× locally.

- **Bug 1 — fixture env-var race:** 3 smoke host fixtures (`ApiHostFixture`, `AuthServerHostFixture`, `SeederSmokeFixture`) mutated the process-global `ConnectionStrings__Default` env var to target their own Testcontainer; multi-host boot in one process raced those writes. Fixed with new `UseTestConnectionStrings` extension (`tests/shared/AqtCoreFW.Tests.SharedFixtures/TestConnectionStringHostBuilderExtensions.cs`) using `builder.UseSetting(...)` (per-host config) instead of a process-global env var.
- **Bug 2 — Hangfire static storage frozen across hosts:** static `RecurringJob.AddOrUpdate` binds `JobStorage.Current` once per process, so the first-booted host wins and later hosts in the multi-host smoke suite register against an already-disposed Testcontainer. Gated the boot-path recurring-job registration behind new config flag `Hangfire:RegisterRecurringJobs` (`src/host/AqtCoreFW.Api/Program.cs`, default `true`, prod unchanged); the 2 Api-booting smoke fixtures set it `false`.
- **Bug 3 — AuthServer DI regression (real prod bug, not test-infra):** commit `fa0faff2` added `AuditEntryPersister` as an `AuditService` ctor dependency; AuthServer's manual audit registration block (`src/host/AqtCoreFW.AuthServer/Program.cs`) wasn't updated to match, so any audited login (`AuthorizationController`/`ExternalLoginController`/`MfaChallengeController`) would hit a DI activation failure — a 4th recurrence of the pattern already tracked in `docs/dependency-map.md` ("AuthServer Host DI Registration": v2.133p3, v2.137-P7, Slice 1B-2). It was masked until this slice because the smoke gate was already red from bugs #1/#2 and never exercised a real login path. Fixed: `builder.Services.AddScoped<AuditEntryPersister>();` added to AuthServer's manual audit block. **This is the value-proof of the smoke gate** — it caught a real prod regression, not just test-infra flake.
- **New tests:** `FixtureConnectionStringIsolationTests.cs` — hostile-env invariant (fixture boot unaffected by a pre-set conflicting env var) + a static-source guard against reintroducing global env-var mutation in fixture files.
- **Verify:** smoke suite 11/11 GREEN, 3 local runs. Code-review APPROVE, 0 Critical/0 High.
- **CI note:** user has GitHub Actions disabled by choice (Free-tier cost, solo dev) and is keeping it disabled — CI-observed green is explicitly NOT the closure bar here; local-verify (11/11 ×3) is.
- **Contract:** none — test-infra + 1 additive config flag (prod default unchanged) + 1 missing prod DI registration restored. No API/DTO/schema change.

**Type:** feat (persistence + observability) · commit pending · completeness-matrix cell #7 ("Audit-chain under distribution") slice-2, FU of `MSVC-CELL7-TAIL-WATERMARK` · code-review REQUEST_CHANGES → all blockers resolved in-slice.

- **Vấn đề đóng (L1 ingestion-loss):** `AuditBehavior.cs` chạy AUDIT SAU KHI business command đã commit; catch cũ chỉ `LogWarning` rồi nuốt lỗi (không rethrow, không retry) — 1 audit-write fail = mất VĨNH VIỄN sự kiện, không ai biết. Chỉ khi CẢ HAI thất bại (persist + enqueue) mới rethrow → `AuditBehavior` nâng `LogWarning`→`LogCritical` + đếm `audit.ingestion.lost`. Fail-open contract giữ nguyên (audit fail không chặn business command).

Additive: `IBackgroundAuditJobEnqueuer.EnqueueIngestionRetry` (+`HangfireAuditJobEnqueuer` impl), `AuditLogEntry.Rehydrate` domain factory, `OpenTelemetryConfiguration.AddMeter("AqtCoreFW.Audit")`.
- **Review-fixed in-slice (đều false-green dưới sa/db_owner test):** **C1 (Critical):** retry job chạy trong Hangfire scope không có ambient tenant → write cần pin TenantId của ROW (không phải ambient) vào SESSION_CONTEXT, nếu không RLS BLOCK từ chối INSERT named-tenant dưới prod least-priv login → `AuditEntryPersister` mở UoW bằng `BeginAsync(entry.TenantId)`; chứng minh bởi test non-`db_owner` mới `AuditIngestionRecoveryLeastPrivilegeTests` (có non-vacuity guard). **M1:** insert-rồi-catch unique-key = success idempotent (RLS FILTER ẩn read-first dedup dưới least-priv, không SESSION_CONTEXT cho job nền).

## Decision — Kill Isolation Seam (Red-Team), Re-scope to EF-First Read-Isolation Plan (2026-07-13, microservices governance, docs+plan-only)

**Type:** Architecture decision recording (0 code) · validated plan `plans/260713-1720-logical-isolation-connection-resolver-seam` (gitignored) · follows the same-day FU-C defer (below).

- **Approach killed by red-team.** A brainstorm→plan chain for logical isolation proposed a behavior-preserving `IDbConnectionResolver` seam over `DatabaseOptions.ConnectionString`. A 3-lens red-team (4 Critical, source-verified) disproved it: UoW-active reads short-circuit to the shared write connection (`DapperReadDbConnection.cs:94-97`); EF LINQ reads bypass the seam (`AsNoTracking` 195×); the audit HMAC read path opens raw ADO on `GetConnectionString("Default")` (`HmacChainService.cs:369,585`). The seam isolated nothing. Plus a Critical DI defect (AuthServer skips `AddInfrastructure`, `Program.cs:229` — `ValidateOnBuild=false` hides it).
- **Over-correction blocked by threat-model reframe.** "Break the UoW wall" (distributed-tx/saga to isolate UoW-active reads) was rejected: reads inside a coordinated cross-module UoW are part of an operation with authority over both schemas (not cross-service snooping) and dissolve at physical extraction — breaking write-atomicity for ~0 compliance benefit.
- **Re-scoped (validated):** an EF-first read-isolation vertical slice for the `[audit]` boundary — isolate EF (per-context login) + `HmacChainService`, proven by a non-`db_owner` test (DENY `[audit]`, SqlException 229). Standalone-Dapper isolation deferred to a keyed-DI (`[FromKeyedServices]`) follow-on increment. UoW-active + admin/db_owner reads = documented ADR-012 exceptions. Login provisioning reuses the C3 pattern.
- **Lesson (memory `feedback-isolation-seam-must-cover-all-invariant-paths`):** a seam over one connection point ≠ isolation unless ALL runtime read paths funnel through it — enumerate every path before claiming coverage.

## Decision — Defer S4 Extraction; Reserve Physical Extraction for S1/S2 (2026-07-13, microservices governance, docs-only)

## Hardening — Cross-Schema SQL Scanner Now Covers Write-Side Coupling (2026-07-10, architecture guard, test-only)

**Type:** Architecture-guard completeness · defense-in-depth · build 0W/0E · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS.

**Summary:** Completed the write-side blind spot in `CrossSchemaSqlScanner` (the arch-test helper that guards the module→schema boundary for microservices extraction). The scanner previously flagged only read-side cross-schema SQL (`FROM`/`JOIN <schema>.`) and was blind to write-side references (`UPDATE`/`INSERT [INTO]`/`MERGE [INTO] <schema>.`) — a cross-schema write couples module ownership harder than a read, so the write side was the more dangerous half to leave open. **Scope note (INVARIANT 260522-A audit):** the original backlog ask ("route genuine request-path coupling") was a no-op — the 3 real couplings were refactored to ModuleClient interfaces at v2.132p10; the whitelist is 6 install-time seeders + 2 read-only D7 dashboard queries, all legitimate. Empirical probe confirmed all 20 raw-SQL sites are owner-local (0 cross-schema writes today), so this catches 0 current violations — pure regression-prevention for the locked extraction goal (`MSVC-5SVC-TARGET`). **Change (test-project only, no `src/` change):** broadened the shared keyword alternation in the two existing regexes to include the write verbs (INTO optional per T-SQL, leading `\b` word-boundary anchor); the pre-existing `KnownSchemas` filter keeps the broadening false-positive-safe. Added 7 non-vacuous self-tests (`CrossSchemaSqlScannerTests`) that drive the real `Scan()` entrypoint over a temp module tree — positive per write verb + read regression guard + owned-schema + whitelisted-file negatives. **Verify:** Architecture.Tests 168/168 (was 161; +7 self-tests), the real-tree scan `NoModule_Should_Reference_AnotherModuleSchema_InRawSql` stays green (0 false positives introduced), build 0W/0E. **Contract:** none — test helper only; stricter detection is additive. **Nits (deferred, pre-existing):** inline trailing comments still scanned; scanner dedup doc slightly overstates behavior. Interpolated-schema `FromSqlRaw` detection remains out of scope (documented limitation).

## Correctness — Global Uniqueness for Public-Forms Cross-Tenant Code Resolution (2026-07-09, Forms module, index + guard)

**Type:** Correctness hardening · database index · application guard · build 0W/0E · code-review DONE.

**Summary:** Locked cross-tenant public-forms by-Code resolution to deterministic global uniqueness. **Root cause (latent, pre-existing):** Anonymous public-forms read handlers (`GetPublicFormQueryHandler`, `SubmitPublicFormCommandHandler`, `GetPublicSignatureDocHashQueryHandler`) resolve by-Code under the `public_forms_bypass` session flag with `QueryFirstOrDefault` + no ORDER BY. Existing `(TenantId, Code)` unique index allows two tenants to each own Active+IsPublic=1 templates with the same Code → resolution is arbitrary (could serve either tenant). **NOT a data-leak** (only IsPublic=1 rows visible) + **NOT introduced** by this session (same cross-tenant lookup already ran under `sa`/db_owner in production). **Design:** Global uniqueness of PUBLIC codes (user confirmed "are public Codes globally-unique" = YES). **Fix:** (1) Migration `20260709082745_AddFormTemplatePublicCodeUniqueIndex` — filtered unique index `UX_FormTemplate_PublicCode ON forms.FormTemplates(Code) WHERE IsPublic = 1 AND IsDeleted = 0` (declared in `FormTemplateConfiguration`, EF-model-as-truth). (2) Fail-loud pre-flight: migration includes safety abort using `STRING_AGG` of colliding Codes → `THROW 50000` if the DB already has cross-tenant public-Code dupes (never auto-demotes a tenant, non-destructive). (3) App-guard in `SetFormTemplatePublicAccessCommandHandler` — when enabling IsPublic on a Code already public in another tenant, returns HTTP **409** with `FormErrors.PublicCodeConflict` (new code **GOV_FRM_019**). Uses `public_forms_bypass` Dapper probe (NOT EF `AnyAsync`) because Forms RLS FILTER hides cross-tenant rows from tenant-pinned admin login under least-privilege. (4) Doc-only: note added to `IReadDbConnection.QueryFirstOrDefaultWithPublicFormsBypassAsync` explaining the bypass context. **Contract-stable:** PATCH `.../public-access` endpoint, `SetFormTemplatePublicAccessCommand`, `FormTemplateDto`, 3 public by-Code SQLs, per-tenant (TenantId, Code) index all unchanged. **Verify:** build 0W/0E, Forms.Integration 67/67 (2 new + 22 regression + 43 broad), PublicFormsLeastPrivilegeTests 8/8 (incl. new least-priv guard-probe test).

## Security — Anonymous Public-Forms RLS Carve-Out (2026-07-09, Forms/RLS, least-privilege blocker)

**Type:** Security hardening · RLS policy · least-privilege read carve-out · build 0W/0E · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS.

**Summary:** Fixed critical RLS blocker preventing anonymous public-forms reads under least-privilege (non-`db_owner`) DB login. Previously, `forms.FormTemplates` RLS FILTER (`fn_TenantFilter: IS_MEMBER('db_owner') OR TenantId=SESSION_CONTEXT('TenantId')`) returned 0 rows when SESSION_CONTEXT unset (anonymous) + non-db_owner login, causing all 3 anonymous public-forms read paths (template-by-Code resolution for GET/POST/signature-hash-query) to fail 404 before reaching the now-pinned writes. Worked only under `sa` (db_owner bypasses RLS) — false-green. **Design:** Asymmetric RLS policy carve-out per `FormTemplate.IsPublic` flag. **NEW:** (1) `FormTemplate.IsPublic` bool column (default false, migration backfills Active templates → IsPublic=1); (2) Asymmetric RLS: FILTER fn `fn_forms_FormTemplates_TenantFilter(@TenantId, @IsPublic)` adds `OR (IsPublic=1 AND SESSION_CONTEXT('public_forms_bypass')='true')`; separate BLOCK fn `fn_forms_FormTemplates_TenantInsertGuard` (IsPublic flag never touches INSERT, immutable after creation). (3) New `IReadDbConnection.QueryFirstOrDefaultWithPublicFormsBypassAsync` (Dapper, sets session context, dedicated connection, pool reset clears bypass) for by-Code lookup; new `IFormTemplateRepository.GetPublicWithFieldsAsync` (EF, pins SESSION_CONTEXT to resolved tenant) for second-step read. (4) 3 public command/query handlers updated: `GetPublicFormQueryHandler`, `SubmitPublicFormCommandHandler`, `GetPublicSignatureDocHashQueryHandler` (each routes by-Code SQL through bypass read, then tenant-aware read, with `AND IsPublic=1` guard). **Migrations:** `20260709033410_AddFormTemplateIsPublic` + `20260709033527_AddFormTemplatePublicReadRlsCarveOut`. **Tests:** New `PublicFormsLeastPrivilegeTests` (6 cases, under rls_test_app non-db_owner context, A/B non-vacuous assertions) + fixture GRANT on forms tables. Build 0W/0E, Forms.Application 340+, Architecture 158, 1,791 tests PASS. **Impact:** Anonymous public-forms unblocked under least-privilege login. NEW templates default IsPublic=0 (not anonymously addressable until admin-toggle ships); existing Active templates backfilled IsPublic=1 (backward-compatible). **Follow-ups:** `PUBLIC-FORMS-ISPUBLIC-ADMIN-TOGGLE` (T4, admin API + FE toggle to make templates public) and `PUBLIC-FORMS-CODE-GLOBAL-UNIQUENESS` (T4, product-Q on by-Code global uniqueness).

## Security — Kubernetes NetworkPolicy Egress Exfil Hole Narrowed (2026-07-09, Infrastructure/Helm)

**Type:** Security hardening · Kubernetes network policy · build 0W/0E · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS.

**Summary:** Narrowed critical egress exfil vulnerability in Helm `infra/helm/aqtcorefw/templates/network-policy.yaml`. Previously, egress rules for ports 443/4317/4318 lacked `to:` selectors, admitting traffic to ANY destination over TLS and OTEL ports, contradicting the default-deny posture claimed by `policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]`. **Fix:** (1) External HTTPS 443 (Keycloak IdP + remote signing providers) → parameterized per-CIDR allowlist via new Helm values `networkPolicy.egress.httpsCidrs[]` (when populated, renders strict `to: ipBlock` rules; empty by default → one documented fallback to any-443 until mesh-pilot enables FQDN egress filtering). (2) OTEL collector ports 4317/4318 → gated behind `networkPolicy.egress.otel.enabled` (default false → no render; zero collectors wired today) + scoped to collector's namespace. (3) DNS 53 remains broad (intentional). **Architecture guard:** New `NetworkPolicyEgressGuardTests` (3 static-parse facts) asserts no to:-less rules remain (prevents future regression). **Verify:** build 0W/0E, Architecture.Tests 161/161, code-review 0 blockers. **Impact:** Default render provably strictly tighter than pre-fix; no new egress opened.

No logic change; no cross-module contract change (dependency-map unaffected).
