## Feature — Signing Foundation Phase 2c-C: Sign an Uploaded PDF from the Files Page (2026-06-17)

**Type:** feature (BE Files module + FE) · `/cook Phase 2 → 2c-C` · resolves the reported UX gap "no sign button after uploading a PDF". Part of the Phase 2 (USB PDF remaining) decomposition; 2c-A (form-gen consumer) + 2c-B (anchor placement) still pending, 2c-D (cert-bind verify) blocked on the Phase 6 sandbox.

**Summary:** A user can now USB-sign an already-uploaded PDF directly from the Files page. Previously signing existed only as a form-field widget (signs form *data*) — there was no surface to sign an uploaded file. The provider-agnostic signing entry point + the `UploadedPdf` DocFlow route were already shipped; this slice adds the missing **consumer** (a thin BE staging copy) and the **FE wiring**.

**Changes:**
- **BE staging (Files module):** `StageFileForSigning` command/handler/validator + `POST /api/v1/files/{id}/stage-for-signing` (`[Authorize]` + `[RequiresMfa]`, tenant-scoped). Copies the file bytes from the upload bucket (`aqtcorefw-files`) to the signing-original bucket (`signing-original`) under a tenant-prefixed key `{tenantId}/{docId}.pdf`, mints a docId, returns `{docId, originalStorageKey}`. **Why the copy is required:** the DocFlow download reads the unsigned original from `signing-original`, not the upload bucket — a direct key reference would 404. Rejects non-PDF (server-side, in addition to the FE gate) and non-`Available` (still-scanning) files; streams disposed; no PDF parsing.
- **FE refactor (DRY, no behaviour change):** `vgca-docflow-methods.ts` extracted `runVgcaPlugin` (plugin-invocation core) + `signTypeToPluginFn`; the 7 existing DocFlow methods still initiate-then-invoke unchanged. This lets the uploaded-PDF path drive the ceremony from the unified `createSigningRequest` handoff **without a second `/initiate` call** (avoids a duplicate signing record).
- **FE feature:** `file-signing-api`, `use-sign-uploaded-file` hook (stage → `createSigningRequest(UploadedPdf)` → `runVgcaPlugin` → poll `useSigningRequestStatus` → invalidate the files list), and `sign-uploaded-file-modal` (provider gate, agent probe + install CTA, minimal metadata form: signType/docNumber/issuedDate, cert-not-verified caveat restated on success). A "Ký số" action on the Files page, gated on `contentType === 'application/pdf'` **and** a `Clean` scan status (avoids a dead click while a scan is pending).
- **Security (documented gap):** an uploaded USB-signed PDF is stored and shown as signed **without** cert==signer verification — the signer cert lives inside the PDF and verifying it requires parsing, deferred to Phase 2c-D / the Phase 6 sandbox. The caveat is surfaced in the signing UI (during signing and on success) and in the plan/release notes; the PDF is not presented as fully verified.

**Verified:** BE 126/126 (Files.Application, incl. 12 new staging tests: tenant-mismatch, non-Available, non-PDF, copy-source/dest/key-shape) · FE 1114/1114 (incl. refactor-regression suite proving no double-initiate + the sign-flow suite + a new PDF-and-Clean gate test) · tsc 0 · eslint 0 (changed files) · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS (Nit-5 finding-code comment fixed; Low-2 scan-gate + Low-3 success-caveat applied; Low-4 in-modal retry-after-plugin-failure deferred as a non-blocking follow-up). A form template can declare named signer roles; a multi-signer submission captures per-signer evidence in an additive child collection while the existing single-signer scalar path stays byte-for-byte unchanged. **Additive-first** throughout (user-locked decision): the 6 scalar evidence columns + `RecordSignatureEvidence` are retained; the collection is added alongside.

**Changes:**
- **Schema (child tables, mirror `FormField→FormFieldOption`):** NEW `FormTemplateSignerRole` (`RoleKey`, `RoleLabelVi`, `DisplayOrder`, `IsRequired`, `PlacementJson`) on `FormTemplate` via `SignerRoles` nav + `AddSignerRole(...)` (mirrors `AddField` Active-version-bump). ## Feature — Signing Foundation Phase 2b: Multi-Signer Transport + BP Sign-Document Gate (2026-06-17)

**Type:** feature (BE Identity + BusinessProcess + SharedKernel.Contracts) · `/cook Phase 2b` · 2 of 3 sub-slices shipped, Forms sub-slice deferred.

**Summary:** Built the marquee net-new multi-signer signing capability — previously there was no transport for more than one signer and no link between BusinessProcess and signing. Shipped in reviewable sub-slices: **2b-1** incremental-chaining transport (Identity), **2b-2** BP "sign document" gate + signing-session aggregate. **2b-3** (Forms signer-role schema + multi-signer evidence) shipped subsequently the same day once Docker was available — see the Phase 2b-3 entry above.

**2b-1 — Incremental-chaining transport** (`5235098a`): A single PDF can be signed by ≥2 signers in strict sequence on the USB DocFlow path — signer N+1 signs signer N's output (incremental PAdES; BE never rewrites the PDF). Added `SignerSequenceNumber` + `PreviousSignedStorageKey` to `SigningDocFlowRecord`/`SigningRequest` (additive, default sequence 1 → existing single-sign unchanged); `InitiateDocFlowCommand` validator requires a tenant-prefixed previous key when sequence > 1; `FileUploadHandlerController.Download` serves the prior signed PDF for sequence > 1; `SignatureOrchestrator` rejects starting round N until round N-1 is terminal-Completed (typed result, not a throw). `isFirstSignature` is server-derived. Migration `signing_incremental_chain`.

**2b-2 — BP sign-document gate + session** (`68722b02`): A BP transition can require M-of-N (default all-of-N) named signers in sequence; the handler short-circuits with a `RequiresMoreSignatures(nextSigner)` outcome (sibling to the existing form-gate, resolved as a read before the single-connection unit of work — no new DTC path) until satisfied. New `DocumentSignatureSession` aggregate (ordered signer slots, threshold, PendingVerify blocks the gate) lives in **Identity**; BusinessProcess reaches it only via the new `IDocumentSignatureSessionClient` contract (module isolation preserved). Transport hardening (now that sequence > 1 is reachable): a **filtered-active unique index** on `(TenantId, DocId, SignerSequenceNumber)` + **supersede-on-reinit** in the same `SaveChanges` — prevents two concurrent inits at the same sequence while still allowing a single-signer retry after an abandoned/expired prior attempt; a unique-constraint violation is caught and returned as a typed conflict (4xx, not 500). Migration `signature_session`.

**Verified:** build 0E/0W (`src/AqtCoreFW.slnx`). Identity.Domain 81/81 · Identity.Application 318/318 · BusinessProcess.Application 115/115 · Architecture 109/109 (MigrationConsistency + ModuleIsolation) · 15 new 2b-2 signing unit/concurrency tests pass · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS. **Known verification gaps (Docker daemon unavailable this session — environmental, not regressions; 2b-1's Integration was 269/269 with Docker up):** Identity.Integration + TenantIsolation RLS suites unverified; supersede atomicity + unique-violation only exercised on EF InMemory (re-run against real SQL when Docker is up). **Follow-ups:** (1) RLS policies for the two new `DocumentSignatureSessions`/`DocumentSignatureSessionSigners` tables (app-layer TenantId guard present, no active leak; required before production least-privilege cutover); (2) the Forms sub-slice 2b-3 — **shipped same day** (see Phase 2b-3 entry above; the Integration/InMemory gap noted here is **closed** there — real-SQL Identity.Integration 269/269 + the `NOT IN`→`IN (0,1)` filtered-index fix). ## Fix — Audit Chain Stale Backlog + Recurring Sweep Job (2026-06-16)

**Type:** fix (BE Audit module, Hangfire recurring job) · backlog `AUDIT-CHAIN-STALE-BACKLOG-SWEEP` (closed).

**Summary:** `/cook` of a production health-check outage. The `/health/ready` endpoint's `audit-unsigned-backlog` check reported "Unhealthy" due to 4 NULL-tenant (system audit chain) rows stuck at `SequenceId=0`, age ~12 days > the 10-minute threshold assumed by the check. Root cause: audit-chain signing was driven purely by enqueue-on-append; the dormant NULL-tenant chain received no new appends for 12 days, so the background sign job was never triggered. There was no recurring sweeper.

**Changes:** new recurring Hangfire job `AuditChainSweepJob` (`HmacChainService.EnqueueSignForBackloggedChainsAsync`) enqueued every 5 minutes on the `default` queue (startup + recurring via `RecurringJob.AddOrUpdate`). The job reads all tenant chains (incl. NULL) with SequenceId=0 backlog via the admin/db_owner connection and enqueues an incremental sign per backlogged tenant. Enqueue-only (idempotent; writes no audit entry, avoiding chain-fork/backfill-loop) — signing itself is the existing per-tenant enqueue-sign pattern via applock. Scope: heals SequenceId=0 stuck-at-initial state only; seq>0/empty-sig is unreachable-by-construction (routed to manual admin backfill if corruption). New files: `AuditChainSweepJob.cs` (new), `HmacChainService.EnqueueSignForBackloggedChainsAsync` (new private `ReadBackloggedTenantIdsAsync` helper). Doc-fix on `UnsignedAuditBacklogHealthCheckOptions` (the "5-minute recurring schedule" the threshold assumed now exists).

**Verified:** post-deploy+restart the nudge signed the 4 NULL rows (SequenceId 1-4) and global unsigned backlog reached 0 → `/health/ready` = Healthy. Build 0W/0E · HmacChain integration 18/18 (+3 new) · Audit unit 20/20 · code-review **APPROVE_WITH_NITS** (M1 scope documented as intentional — sweep handles SequenceId=0 only; seq>0 corruption requires manual admin backfill).

**Linked:** files `src/modules/audit/AqtCoreFW.Audit.Infrastructure/{Services/HmacChainService.cs, Jobs/AuditChainSweepJob.cs, InfrastructureRegistration.cs, HealthChecks/UnsignedAuditBacklogHealthCheckOptions.cs}`, `tests/integration/AqtCoreFW.Audit.Integration.Tests/HmacChainSweepTests.cs` (new).

## Fix — File-Upload & Virus-Scan UX: Silent-Error Toast + Scan-Timeout Fallback (2026-06-16)

**Type:** fix (FE `forms`/`files`) · backlog `POLISH-D-FILE-UPLOAD-SCAN-UX` (closed). FE-only, 0 BE↔FE contract change.

**Summary:** `/cook` Theme D of the Workflow/Forms/BP polish-audit. Audit-at-slice-start (INVARIANT 260522-A) read the live code at the row's 2 sites: **Defect 1's premise was inaccurate** (the failed upload was fully silent, not "red badge no toast" — `showUploadList={false}` suppresses antd's error item and the lifecycle stepper renders nothing on error); **Defect 2 confirmed** (a stuck virus scan froze the stepper indefinitely).

**Defect 1 — surface the upload failure:** `FileFieldWidget.onError` (`form-field-renderer.tsx`) now calls `appMessage.error(extractApiErrorMessage(error) ?? t('forms.field.uploadFailed'))` — DRY-reuses the `extract-api-error.ts` util shipped in POLISH-B, which returns `undefined` for non-API rejections (bare JS Errors) so internal messages never leak. The dead `setFileList([{status:'error'}])` line (invisible under `showUploadList={false}`) was removed.

**Defect 2 — scan-timeout fallback:** `useFileScanStatus` (`file-api.ts`) previously stopped polling at the 30-attempt cap (~60s) with no terminal signal when clamd was unreachable (status stuck `Quarantined`). It now returns `{ ...query, timedOut, retryScan }`: `timedOut = Boolean(fileId) && !isTerminal && attempts >= cap` (attempts read via `queryClient.getQueryState` — the same `dataUpdateCount + fetchFailureCount` counter the `refetchInterval` gate uses, so it resolves on the final poll's completion render); `retryScan` calls `resetQueries` to re-poll from attempt 0 (a lone `refetch()` would tick the counter past the cap and the gate would immediately re-stop). A new `'timeout'` `FilePhase` (`file-lifecycle-steps.tsx`) renders the scan step red (antd `Steps` has no `warning` status) and is checked **after** the `Available`/`Rejected` verdicts so a late terminal status still wins; the widget renders a warning `Text` + "Thử lại" button below the stepper. The uploaded `fileId` is intentionally kept on timeout (the scan may still resolve) — not cleared.

**Cross-consumer blast radius (verified nil):** the additive hook return doesn't disturb `form-attachment-preview.tsx` / `file-list-page.tsx` (read only `.data`); the new optional 4th `deriveFilePhase` param defaults `false`, so `file-list-page.tsx:191` is unchanged. Files-page uploader adopting the same fallback is an optional out-of-scope follow-up.

**Verified:** tsc app 0E · eslint 0E (2 pre-existing react-refresh warnings) · vitest files+forms 101/101 (+6 new `deriveFilePhase` timeout/precedence tests, verified in isolation ×2 — no flake) · code-review **APPROVE** (0 Critical/High/Medium; 2 Low nits left YAGNI).

**Type:** fix (BE `forms` + FE `business-process`/`workflow` + `core/api`) · backlog `POLISH-B-SWALLOWED-EXCEPTIONS` (closed) → files `SIGN-WFLINK-RETRY-CREATE-IDEMPOTENT`, `EXTRACT-API-ERROR-CODE-DEDUP`.

**Summary:** `/cook` Theme B of the Workflow/Forms/BP polish-audit. Audit-at-slice-start (INVARIANT 260522-A, 9th payoff) read the live code at the row's 5 claimed sites and reclassified them: **2 were stale/not-a-defect**, **3 FE swallows + 1 BE asymmetry were real**.

**Reclassified OUT (no change):** (1) `SubmitFormCommandHandler.cs:251` "silent orphan" — line 251 is the success-branch `UpdateAsync`; the rejection-orphan is already surfaced via `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingEvent`, not silent. (2) `StartBusinessProcessRunCommandHandler.cs:139` "Forms error masked as 'BP không tìm thấy'" — `ToFailureResult` emits that string only for `CrossTenantRejected` (intentional 404 no-existence-leak); Forms field errors are preserved as 422 per-field.

**BE — close throw-orphan asymmetry:** `SubmitFormCommandHandler` + `SubmitPublicFormCommandHandler` previously published `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingEvent` only on the `!IsSuccess` rejection branch; the `catch (Exception)` hard-throw branch only logged, so throw-orphans (broker/network/timeout, or a link-write throw after a created instance) were invisible to the ops/admin pending-link handler. Both catch branches now publish the same event with a new canonical `FormSubmissionWorkflowLinkPendingEvent.ExceptionFailureCode = "WF_LINK_EXCEPTION"`. Downstream handler is idempotent (UPSERT) + fail-soft, so emitting inside catch cannot disturb the already-committed submit response. The event XML-doc carries a consumer-note: `WF_LINK_EXCEPTION` may be a created-but-unlinked instance, so any retry consumer must be create-idempotent (tracked as `SIGN-WFLINK-RETRY-CREATE-IDEMPOTENT`).

**FE — surface the backend reason:** new `web/src/core/api/extract-api-error.ts` (`extractApiErrorMessage`/`extractApiErrorCode`) reads both the `NormalizedApiError` interceptor shape and the raw axios envelope, and returns `undefined` for antd `validateFields` rejections + bare JS Errors so internal messages never leak to a toast. Wired into `allowed-actions-bar.tsx` (transition `catch {}` → backend reason), `definition-webhook-config-tab.tsx` (split `validateFields` → silent inline from the mutation catch → surfaced), and `definition-assignment-rules-tab.tsx` (added try/catch to handleDelete + handleCreate — previously NONE, so a rejected mutation became an unhandled promise rejection with no toast).

## Feature — DocFlow Orphan Signed-Blob Sweep (2026-06-16)

**Type:** feature (BE, Files.Domain + Files.Infrastructure + Api host) · backlog `SIGN-DOCFLOW-ORPHAN-BLOB-SWEEP`.

**Summary:** `/cook` of the Slice-1 (H3) review L2 follow-up. The VGCA doc-flow upload writes the signed PDF to bucket `signing-docflow` under a random-GUID key BEFORE committing `record.Complete()`; a lost concurrency race (or process crash) strands an unreferenced blob whose key was never persisted (`SignedStorageKey` stays null). Audit-at-slice-start found the row undersold scope: because the orphan key only ever lived in the failed request's memory, a DB-only sweep is impossible — the sweep must enumerate the bucket, but `IFileStorageService` exposed only Upload/Download/Delete. Surfaced the scope to the user, who chose the additive-sweep approach.

**Changes:**
- `IFileStorageService` gains `ListObjectsAsync(bucket, prefix)` + a `StorageObjectInfo(Key, LastModified, Size)` record (Files.Domain); `MinioFileStorageService` implements it via Minio 6.0.4 `ListObjectsEnumAsync` (bucket-absent → empty list, skips directory markers).
- New `SigningDocFlowOrphanBlobSweepJob` in the **Api host** (cross-module — it needs both `IdentityDbContext` and `IFileStorageService`; placed in the host like `FileUploadHandlerController` to avoid an Identity→Files dependency). It lists the bucket, groups objects by their `{tenantId}/` key prefix, and per tenant pins the DB `SESSION_CONTEXT` to that tenant before reading referenced `SignedStorageKey`s (so RLS returns the full set under a future least-privilege login), then deletes blobs older than a 24h grace window that no record references. Registered daily at 03:00 UTC on the `default` queue (no new `BackgroundJobQueues` constant, so the queue-registration arch guard is unaffected).

**Deletion-safety (reviewer-verified across db_owner-today and least-priv-future):** the original unsigned PDFs live in a separate bucket (`signing-original`) so they are never candidates; `IgnoreQueryFilters()` keeps soft-deleted records' blobs counted as referenced; the 24h grace window protects the UploadAsync→Complete in-flight gap; a **circuit-breaker** skips any tenant that has deletion candidates but zero referenced keys (a far more likely sign of a silent reference-load/RLS gap than a genuinely 100%-orphan tenant — never mass-delete on an empty read); `[DisableConcurrentExecution]` + `[AutomaticRetry(Attempts=0)]`.

**Verified:** Files.Infrastructure 0W/0E · Api host 0W/0E (both `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`) · 5 pure-function `SelectOrphanKeys` tests + Files.Infrastructure 37 + Files.Application 114 + Architecture 109 = all green, no regression · code-review APPROVE (DONE_WITH_CONCERNS; both Medium findings — empty-referenced circuit-breaker + AutomaticRetry parity — applied before commit).

## Fix — Enroll Signer-Cert User-Existence + Tenant Guard (2026-06-16)

**Type:** fix (BE, Identity) · backlog `SIGN-ENROLL-USER-EXISTS-CHECK`.

**Summary:** `/cook` of the Slice-3 (C1) review L1 follow-up. `EnrollSignerCertCommandHandler` previously went straight from a duplicate-active-cert check to `AddAsync`, never verifying the target `UserId` — a SystemAdmin typo (the endpoint is SystemAdmin-only, with tenant-override) left an orphan enrollment row bound to no real signer. The handler now resolves the user via `UserManager.FindByIdAsync` **first** and returns `NotFoundError` when the user is missing **or** `user.TenantId != cmd.TenantId`. A single error covers both cases to avoid handing the caller a cross-tenant existence oracle.

**Why the explicit tenant check isn't redundant with RLS:** the endpoint resolves tenant via `ResolveTenantId()` which supports a SystemAdmin override; the RLS session-context is not guaranteed to match that override target, so relying on RLS alone to null-out a cross-tenant `FindByIdAsync` is unsafe. The in-handler `user.TenantId == cmd.TenantId` assertion makes correctness independent of session-context alignment. Threat model is data-integrity (orphan row), not a security hole — RLS still scopes the enrollment row to its own tenant.

**Changes:** `EnrollSignerCertCommand.cs` handler ctor gains `UserManager<ApplicationUser>` + the existence/tenant guard (mirrors `LockUser`/`UpdateUser`); `DigitalSignatureController.EnrollCert` gains `[ProducesResponseType(404)]` (OpenAPI accuracy — `ToApiResponse` already maps `NotFoundError`→404). 5 new `SigningHandlerTests` cases: in-tenant→enroll, missing→404+no-insert, cross-tenant→404+no-insert, global-user (null TenantId)→404+no-insert, duplicate→400 still fires.

**Verified:** Identity.Application unit **308/308** green (5 new) · src `Identity.Application` 0 warnings · code-review APPROVE 0 Crit/High/Med. **Follow-up filed:** `SIGN-ENROLL-TEST-CS4014-FALSEGREEN` (pre-existing un-awaited `DidNotReceive` at `SigningHandlerTests.cs:450` — latent false-green, kept out of this commit to stay focused).

## Signing-core Security Remediation — Phase 0 GATING (2026-06-15)

**Type:** fix (security, shipped signing-core) · commits `be7c0264` / `7cd044bc` / `013b074e` · NOT pushed.

**Summary:** `/cook` of Phase 0 of the document-signing foundation — three verified security defects in the **shipped** signing-core, each gating PDF signing, fixed as 3 independently-green slices. All re-verified empirically against current code before touching shipped code (the red-team report cited drifted file paths). Plan: `plans/260615-1804-document-signing-foundation/phase-00-security-remediation.md`. Journal: `docs/journals/journal-260615-2030-signing-phase0-security-remediation.md`.

**Changes:**
- **H3 — atomic nonce (`be7c0264`):** `SigningDocFlowNonce.TryUse()` was an in-memory `UseCount++` with no DB guard → parallel uploads with the same JWT double-spent the nonce. Added a `RowVersion` optimistic-concurrency token on the nonce + record (mirrors `SigningPendingTransaction`); the handler maps `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`→401; `CHECK(UseCount<=MaxUses)` defence-in-depth. Migration `20260615183000_AddSigningDocFlowRowVersion`.
- **C2 — DocFlow tenant-isolation (`7cd044bc`):** the `[AllowAnonymous]` round-trip carried no tenant in the JWT, loaded record/nonce with no tenant check, trusted an FE-supplied storage key, and stored uploaded bytes as "signed" after only a content-type check. Added a signed `tenant_id` JWT claim + explicit `record/nonce.TenantId == jwt.tenant` asserts + SESSION_CONTEXT-from-JWT (RLS) + `OriginalStorageKey` tenant-prefix validation + server-side `%PDF` magic-byte sniff. RLS (FILTER+BLOCK) on both docflow tables. Full crypto/cert PDF verify deferred to the Phase-6 sandbox.
- **C1 — cert==assigned-signer (`013b074e`):** the anti-impersonation invariant was vaporware (remote fell back to a default account; USB/detached accepted any chain-valid cert). New `SignerCertEnrollment` store (serial+issuer/thumbprint = forge-resistant key) + RLS + admin enroll/list API; `SignerBindingGuard` (verdict, never throws: enrolled-key → CCCD-from-subject bootstrap → else fail-closed, tenant-scoped); remote removed the default-account fallback for user-attributed signing (fail-closed on missing national id) + binds the returned cert (sync + confirm); Forms verify-at-ingest binds the cert to the authenticated submitter (anon public-form path unaffected). Migration `20260615185000_AddSignerCertEnrollment`.

**Operational behavior change:** authed form signing + remote signing now **fail closed** unless the signer has an enrolled cert OR a matching `SigningNationalId` — intended anti-impersonation posture; signer identity provisioning is now a prerequisite.

## Audit HMAC Per-Tenant Chain — Signer-Assigned SequenceId + Backfill + Health Check (2026-06-15)

**Type:** architecture + feature (QĐ 742 tamper-evidence) · `/cook` (P1 HMAC fix).

**Problem:** Previous HMAC chain ordering relied on `AuditLogEntry.InternalId` (DB-assigned insertion order), which could diverge from actual causality if entries were signed out-of-order (e.g., batch commits reordered, async signing latency). This broke chain verification in scenarios with concurrent audit writes.

**Solution — Per-Tenant Independent Chains:**
- **Signer-Assigned SequenceId:** `HmacChainService.SignTenantChainAsync(Guid? tenantId)` now assigns a monotonic `SequenceId` (1, 2, 3, ...) to each unsigned entry within a tenant's chain during signing, reflecting the signer's view of causality, not insertion order. The column is **retained** (not dropped) to anchor the chain order durably.
- **Per-Tenant Signing:** Each tenant (and the NULL system tenant) gets its own independent chain + locking. Different tenants sign in parallel; same-tenant entries serialize via SQL Server `sp_getapplock` on resource `audit-hmac:{tenantKey}` (return-code checked → throws → Hangfire `[AutomaticRetry]` re-runs). No `[DisableConcurrentExecution]` to allow cross-tenant parallelism.
- **Prod Least-Privilege Signer:** The signing job opens a **raw `SqlConnection`** (not pooled) with RLS bypass set BEFORE read: (1) session context `TenantId` = target tenant, (2) session context `audit_mutate_mode` = `'signature'` (allows immutability trigger to write HMACs), (3) reads unsigned, (4) computes HMAC-SHA256 over canonical JSON + prior signature, (5) clears context in finally. New config key **`ConnectionStrings:AuditAdmin`** (db_owner-capable login) used by backfill + health check to enumerate tenants; falls back to `Default` if not set.
- **Backfill Endpoint:** `POST /api/v1/audit/chain/backfill` (SystemAdmin-only, class `Audit.Log.View`). Returns **202 Accepted** + Hangfire job ID. Background job re-signs every tenant's chain (SequenceId 1..N, atomic per tenant). Writes one `chain-backfill` audit entry with actor + timestamp.
- **Health Check:** New `audit-unsigned-backlog` endpoint. Unhealthy if unsigned count > `MaxUnsignedCount` (default 100) OR oldest unsigned age > `MaxOldestUnsignedAge` (default 10 min). Uses elevated `AuditAdmin` connection to read cross-tenant.

**Architecture:**
- `HmacChainService.SignTenantChainAsync(Guid? tenantId, CancellationToken)` — background job entry (called every 5 min per tenant).
- `IHmacChainBackfiller` — new interface for backfill orchestration.
- `IBackgroundAuditJobEnqueuer.EnqueueBackfillChain(Actor actor)` — new method to trigger backfill.
- `UnsignedAuditBacklogHealthCheck` — new health-check service.

**Backward Compatibility:**
- Existing `AuditLogEntry.HmacSignature` column untouched; `SequenceId` column retained (not dropped).
- `VerifyAsync(Guid? tenantId)` unchanged: orders by SequenceId (now signer-assigned, not insertion order) + detects mid-chain holes.
- No API contract change; backfill is a new admin endpoint.
- Existing signed entries keep their (now-stale) `SequenceId` values; backfill re-signs + re-assigns fresh SequenceId per tenant.

**Verified:** Concurrency tests pass (per-tenant lock serializes, cross-tenant parallel) · Least-privilege signer bypasses RLS via session context (no `IsDeleted` filter, full audit view) · Backfill atomicity under transaction (abort rolls back all tenant chains together) · Health check uses elevated connection · code-review APPROVE 0 Critical/High. **Follow-ups:** `FU-HMAC-ROTATION` (add `HmacKeyVersion` column to enable future key rotation without silent signature breakage).

## Viettel Signing — CCCD PII Masked in Diagnostic Logs (2026-06-14)

**Type:** fix (security/compliance) · `/cook` (VIETTEL-CCCD-LOG-PII). QĐ 742 §4.4.a PII-in-logs.

**Problem:** After CCCD-mapping, the Viettel remote-signing `userId` is the signer's 12-digit CCCD (Confidential PII). It was logged in plaintext via `{UserId}` structured-log args across the Viettel signing stack — leaking PII into diagnostic output.

**Fix:** New `internal static SigningLogMasking.MaskUserId(string?)` masks to last-4 (`079201001234` → `***1234`; ≤4 chars → `****`; null/empty → `(none)`). Applied at **all 14 log sites across 4 files** (`ViettelMysignProvider.cs` ×10, `ViettelMysignLoginClient.cs`, `ViettelMysignCertInfoClient.cs`, `ViettelMysignSignHashClient.cs` ×2). Original backlog row understated scope (5 sites/1 file); empirical multiline audit found 14/4 — the 2 SignHashClient sites were nearly missed by line-based grep (multi-line log calls).

**Impact:** No behavior/contract change — log message templates (placeholder names) unchanged, so log-query dashboards stay valid; helper is `internal`; sign/verify/cache logic untouched. Cache-key `mysign:tok:…:{userId}` deliberately out of scope (process-local IMemoryCache, never persisted/logged).

**Verified:** build `TreatWarningsAsErrors` 0W/0E · `SigningLogMasking` unit 7/7 (boundary len 4/5, null, empty, full CCCD) · Identity.Infrastructure suite 217/217 · code-review APPROVE 0 Critical/High. **Follow-up filed:** `VIETTEL-VENDOR-ECHO-LOG-PII` (T4) — latent: raw vendor `{Body}`/`{Error}` logs (StatusPoll, SignHash) would resurface CCCD if Viettel ever echoes it in an error payload (not a current leak).

## ClamAV Config Simplification: Fail-Closed Always + Single Feature Flag (2026-06-14)

**Type:** refactor (security hardening) · `/ck:cook` (CLAMAV-BYPASS-FLAG-COLLAPSE). Configuration knob removal + streamlined fail-closed behavior.

**Removed:** `ClamAvOptions.BypassWhenUnavailable` config boolean. This was a fail-open foot-gun — when true (Benchmark environment only), an unreachable clamd would silently pass files as Clean instead of retrying. The knob is now gone; `ClamAvVirusScanner` is unconditionally **fail-closed**: an unreachable/timeout clamd → `VirusScanResult.Error` (never Clean) → `ClamAvScanJob` throws → Hangfire retry → file stays Quarantined, never deleted.

**Removed appsettings:** `ClamAV` section deleted from `appsettings.Development.json` and `appsettings.Benchmark.json` (no longer needed; `ClamAvOptions` now accepts only `Host`, `Port`, `TimeoutMs` via the default schema).

**Updated startup health check:** `ClamAvStartupHealthCheck` now skips the clamd ping ONLY in the `Benchmark` environment (via `IHostEnvironment.IsEnvironment("Benchmark")`). In all other environments (Development, Staging, Production), the health check probes clamd TCP 3310 and logs the result.

**Single control mechanism:** The only virus-scan configuration is now `feature:files.virus-scan` (DB-backed, runtime-settable, per-tenant). When disabled, `ClamAvScanJob` auto-passes (for demo/test environments). When enabled, the scanner is invoked; if clamd is unreachable, the job retries — a transient infra fault does not delete a possibly-clean file.

**Rationale:** The `Bypass` knob was dead config in practice (seeded true in Benchmark where the feature flag is false anyway, so uploads never invoked scanning). Removing it eliminates a silent fail-open code path and clarifies the single control surface for operators.

**Verify:** API host build 0W/0E `/warnaserror` · Files.Infra.Tests 37/37 (+2 new fail-closed scanner error tests) · Files.Application.Tests 114/114 · integration suite 7/7 · no references remain to `BypassWhenUnavailable` in source/config/tests · code-review APPROVE_WITH_NITS (3 Low cosmetic, zero blocking).

## Audit HMAC-Chain Job → Dedicated `audit` Hangfire Queue + Queue-Registration Guard (2026-06-14)

**Type:** fix + test · `/ck:cook` (`HANGFIRE-AUDIT-QUEUE-ORPHANED`). Inverse of the virus-scan-queue fix below.

**Root cause:** `HangfireAuditJobEnqueuer.EnqueueHmacChain` enqueued via `BackgroundJob.Enqueue<HmacChainService>(…)` with no queue arg → the audit HMAC-chain job ran on `default`, even though `opt.Queues` already listed `"audit"` as a priority-2 lane. The lane (deliberate per the registration comment + QĐ742 tamper-evidence motivation) was orphaned dead config. Not a stuck-job (default is drained) but the priority intent was never realized.

**Fix (user chose WIRE over drop):** added `BackgroundJobQueues.Audit` const; `HangfireAuditJobEnqueuer` now enqueues with `BackgroundJobQueues.Audit`; `opt.Queues` raw `"audit"` → the const (anti-drift, same pattern as virus-scan). The static `BackgroundJob.Enqueue` call is kept (not routed through `IBackgroundJobService`) because `HangfireAuditJobEnqueuer` IS the infrastructure Hangfire adapter behind `IBackgroundAuditJobEnqueuer` — routing it through another abstraction would be adapter-calling-adapter for no isolation gain (code-review confirmed). **Prevention:** new arch guard `BackgroundJobQueueRegistrationTests` asserts every `BackgroundJobQueues` constant is referenced in the server's `opt.Queues` — structurally prevents the stuck-job class (a queue const enqueued to but missing from the server list) that the original virus-scan bug was.

**Verify:** API host build `TreatWarningsAsErrors` 0W/0E · new guard 1/1 · Architecture suite 108/109 (the 1 failure is a pre-existing, unrelated MFA compliance test — zero overlap) · Audit.Application 54/54 · existing `HangfireRegistrationConsistencyTests` still green · code-review APPROVE 0-blocking. **Follow-up (reviewer L2/L3):** `HANGFIRE-WEBHOOK-NORMAL-ORPHANED` — `webhook-normal` is the same orphan smell (listed, never enqueued; guard doesn't catch raw-string queues); audit+virus-scan are now both active higher-priority lanes → include the pair in queue-saturation load tests.

## ClamAV Scan Job → Dedicated `virus-scan` Hangfire Queue (2026-06-14)

**Type:** fix · `/ck:fix`. Follow-up to the ClamAV activation slice below.

**Root cause:** `ClamAvScanJob`'s doc claimed a "virus-scan" queue, but `UploadFileCommandHandler` enqueued through `IBackgroundJobService.Enqueue(Expression)` which has no queue param → Hangfire put the job on the `default` queue, and `virus-scan` wasn't even in the processing server's `opt.Queues`. (Latent, not user-visible — `default` is drained — but the dedicated lane the doc promised didn't exist.)

**Fix (6 files):** new shared constant `BackgroundJobQueues.VirusScan` (SharedKernel.Application) used by BOTH the enqueue call site AND the server's `opt.Queues` list — a name mismatch between those two is exactly what would leave a job enqueued on a queue no worker drains (stuck Quarantined forever), so sharing one constant makes that drift a compile-time impossibility. Added a queue-aware overload `IBackgroundJobService.Enqueue<T>(string queue, Expression<Func<T,Task>>)` (→ `BackgroundJob.Enqueue(queue, …)`) instead of a Hangfire `[Queue]` attribute on `IClamAvScanJob` — the interface lives in `Files.Application`, which has no Hangfire ref, and the abstraction's contract is "modules call this interface, not Hangfire directly". `virus-scan` inserted into `opt.Queues` between `audit` and `background` (priority above generic background work, below webhook/audit).

**Verify:** API + AuthServer + Files.Application.Tests build `TreatWarningsAsErrors` 0W/0E · Files.Application 114/114 (updated `Handle_ValidFile_EnqueuesClamAvScanJob_OnVirusScanQueue` asserts the constant, not a literal) · runtime: Hangfire `/hangfire/servers` confirms the server now drains `virus-scan` · code-review APPROVE 0-blocking. **Follow-up (reviewer INFO-1):** `HANGFIRE-AUDIT-QUEUE-ORPHANED` — the `audit` queue is the inverse case (server-listed but `HangfireAuditJobEnqueuer` enqueues to `default`), filed to backlog.

## ClamAV Into Managed Stack + Dev Virus-Scan Activation (2026-06-14)

**Type:** chore (infra) + fix + feat · `/ck-debug` ("chưa có cấu hình clamAV?") → `/ck:cook` (option B2). Mirrors the prior MinIO-into-compose fix.

**Diagnosis:** ClamAV code was complete (`ClamAvVirusScanner`, `ClamAvScanJob`, startup health check) but clamd was NOT in `docker-compose.yml` (unmanaged infra dep, same class as the MinIO outage), and dev double-bypassed scanning — `feature:files.virus-scan` unseeded (default false) + `ClamAV.BypassWhenUnavailable: true` — so uploads went straight to Available without ever contacting clamd.

**Changes (B2 = plumb + activate in dev):** **(1)** `docker-compose.yml` — new `clamav` service (`clamav/clamav:1.4`, TCP 3310, `clamav_data` volume for signature-DB persistence, `clamdcheck.sh` healthcheck), api gets `ClamAV__Host: clamav` (service hostname inside the network, not localhost) + `depends_on: clamav` (`service_started`, parity with minio). **(2)** `appsettings.Development.json` — `BypassWhenUnavailable: false` (fail-closed in dev). **(3)** `SystemParamSeeder` — injects `IHostEnvironment`, seeds `feature:files.virus-scan=true` **only when `IsDevelopment()`**; prod posture intentionally untouched (flipping it on is deploy-affecting, ops-owned — tracked as follow-up). **(4)** `ClamAvScanJob` — split the verdict branch so a scanner **Error** (clamd unreachable/timeout) throws → Hangfire retry with the file kept **Quarantined**, instead of falling into the reject-and-delete path; **Infected** still rejects+deletes. This is what makes `BypassWhenUnavailable:false` safe — a transient clamd outage no longer destroys a clean file. **(5)** `aqt-runapp` skill — Step 1.7 starts clamav + probes clamd before the API (mirror of MinIO Step 1.6).

**Build/Verify:** SystemParams.Infrastructure + Files.Infrastructure `TreatWarningsAsErrors` 0W/0E · Files.Infrastructure.Tests 35/35 (4 new `ClamAvScanJobTests` pinning the three-way verdict branch incl. the Error→no-delete invariant) · Files.Application.Tests 114/114 · `docker compose config` valid · code-review APPROVE (0 Critical/High; M1 service_healthy→service_started applied, L2 stale doc fixed). **Follow-up:** prod virus-scan flag policy (currently false→silent-bypass, latent NĐ68 gap) + first-boot flag-visibility window (dev-only, self-heals).

`dotnet build src/AqtCoreFW.slnx -c Release /warnaserror` was failing **26×** with `NU1903` — `MessagePack 2.5.187` carries high-severity GHSA-hv8m-jj95-wg3x (LZ4-decompression DoS), pulled transitively via `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.StackExchangeRedis 10.0.0`. ## IpFilterRule Insert-Flip Data Audit — Runbook + Remediation Script (2026-06-12)

**Type:** docs/ops (no app code change) · closes follow-up `IPFILTERRULE-PROD-FLIP-DATA-AUDIT`. Per-env data cleanup procedure for rows flipped by the pre-`ffbe2fac` insert bug.

- **Inverted-query finding:** the originally-filed audit query `WHERE IsBlock=0 OR IsEnabled=0` is backwards — the bug flips `false→true`, so corrupted rows read `1/1` and that query returns the *un-corrupted* rows (false "all clean"). A flipped row is value-indistinguishable from a legit enabled/block rule → no auto-detection; suspect set = every pre-fix row (`CreatedAt < @FixDeployUtc`) + manual reconciliation against intended config.
- **EF UPDATE heal asymmetry:** an UPDATE that *changes* a flag (`true→false`) re-emits and heals; an edit resubmitting the displayed flipped value (`true→true`) is not emitted → `UpdatedAt` is a triage hint, never a filter (filtering it would miss a wrongly-blocked admin CIDR).
- **Cache flush mandatory:** a direct DB UPDATE bypasses command-handler invalidation → `IpFilterMiddleware` serves stale `system:ip-rules` for its 5-min TTL → remediation must flush the key (or wait out TTL).
- **Deliverables:** `docs/ops/ipfilterrule-flip-data-audit-runbook.md` + `scripts/260612-ipfilterrule-insert-flip-remediation.sql` (read-only detection + commented per-row remediation template, idempotent). Dev DB re-confirmed 0 rows via sqlcmd; T-SQL validated EXITCODE=0; code-review all-claims-CONFIRMED. AqtCoreFW is a template repo with no live prod — execution is downstream ops per-env.

## ExternalIdentity Re-Link-After-Unlink Fix — Soft-Delete Index Filtering (2026-06-11)

**Type:** fix (schema, unique-index isolation on soft-delete) · `20260611170000_FilterExternalIdentityUniqueIndexesOnSoftDelete` migration + Designer · `src/modules/identity/…/Configurations/ExternalIdentityConfiguration.cs`, `tests/integration/…/ExternalIdentityRelinkAfterUnlinkTests.cs`, `docs/dependency-map.md`.

Closes `soft-delete-filter-on-GetByIdAsync` (reframed from a latent read-side concern to a real index-level bug). The original premise was largely a non-issue: `ExternalIdentityConfiguration` inherits `EntityTypeConfigurationBase.ConfigureSoftDelete`, which applies a GLOBAL query filter `HasQueryFilter(x => !x.IsDeleted)`. All EF repository reads (GetById, dup-check, JIT lookup) **already exclude soft-deleted rows** correctly; GetById already returns 404 on deleted; unlink already blocks SSO re-login. No logic changes needed.

**The one real bug:** The two `ExternalIdentity` UNIQUE indexes — `(UserId, Provider)` and `(Provider, ExternalId)` — were **NOT filtered on IsDeleted**. A soft-deleted (unlinked) row kept occupying the unique slot, so re-linking the same provider/external-id after an unlink threw a duplicate-key 500. **Fix:** Added `.HasFilter("[IsDeleted] = 0")` to both unique indexes in `ExternalIdentityConfiguration.cs` (lines 21, 24); new migration `20260611170000_FilterExternalIdentityUniqueIndexesOnSoftDelete` (drops both indexes, recreates as partial unique, no data change); updated `IdentityDbContextModelSnapshot.cs`. New integration test `ExternalIdentityRelinkAfterUnlinkTests` with 3 assertions (re-link-after-unlink succeeds; second active same-provider blocked; DB-level partial-index proof). Build 0W/0E (warn-as-error); re-link integration 3/3; existing ExternalIdentities unit 19/19 (no regression); architecture `MigrationConsistencyTests` 2/2 (Designer-issue fixed); code-review REQUEST_CHANGES (missing Designer) → fixed → clean. Commits NOT yet pushed.

## Audit→Identity Cross-Schema Decoupling via Module Client (2026-06-11)

**Type:** refactor (architecture, tech-debt elimination) · `src/modules/identity/InProcessIdentityModuleClient.cs`, `src/modules/audit/…/GetLoginAudit/*`, `LoginAuditController.cs`, `tests/integration/…/IdentityModuleClientTenantUserIdsTests.cs`, `tests/integration/…/LoginAttemptsTenantIsolationTests.cs`, `tests/integration/Workflow.Integration.Tests/Stubs/*`.

Closes `AUDIT-IDENTITY-CROSSCHEMA-DEBT`, the architectural follow-up from this morning's cross-tenant read leaks fix. The fix introduced a cross-schema coupling: `GetLoginAuditQueryHandler` (Audit module) tenant-isolated `audit.LoginAttempts` via raw `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM [identity].AspNetUsers u WHERE u.Id = la.UserId AND u.TenantId = @CallerTenantId)` — a direct query into the Identity schema flagged by the `ModuleIsolationTests.NoModule_Should_Reference_AnotherModuleSchema_InRawSql` architecture guard (was RED). **Refactored to extract behavior into a module client (behavior-identical, no migration):** new interface `IIdentityModuleClient.GetUserIdsInTenantAsync(Guid tenantId, CancellationToken ct) → IReadOnlyList<Guid>` exposes tenant membership (no lifecycle / soft-delete filtering — output equals the former EXISTS predicate set). Implementation in `InProcessIdentityModuleClient` executes the same SELECT Id FROM [identity].AspNetUsers WHERE TenantId=@t query locally. Handler injects the client, calls it (non-privileged path only; SystemAdmin still bypasses filtering), serializes the result to JSON, then filters via SQL Server `OPENJSON(@TenantUserIdsJson)` to avoid the ~2100-parameter ceiling a Dapper IN-list would hit for large tenant user sets. Privileged (SystemAdmin) retains cross-tenant view as before. Code-review fixed 1 blocker (param threading) → clean. **Carry-fwd advisory (filed T4, YAGNI now):** `LOGINAUDIT-TENANT-IDS-PERREQ-MATERIALIZE` — non-privileged `GET /login-audit` materializes ALL tenant user-ids per request (admin read-path, low-QPS in practice, no-op until profile shows bottleneck; revisit if hot → consider caching or TVP server-side filter).

**Type:** fix (security, vulnerable dependencies) · `aec38144` (deps) + `f3084908` (test/component hygiene) · `web/package.json`, `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `web/src/features/credential-policies/credential-policies-page.tsx`, `web/src/test/features/{credential-policies/credential-policies-page,smoke-user-pages}.test.tsx`.

A `/security-scan` of the repo found code/secret hygiene clean — Vault-gated production secrets (empty placeholders + `ProductionSecretValidator`), parameterized Dapper SQL throughout (every `{where}` built from constant clause literals, every user value `@`-bound, `SearchTerm` `EscapeSqlLike`-escaped), and zero FE XSS sinks — but flagged 28 frontend dependency advisories. Dependency-tree triage showed the real runtime attack surface is **axios alone**; every other flagged package (fast-uri, ws, brace-expansion) is dev/build tooling (orval codegen, eslint, vitest/jsdom) with no browser exposure. Bumped `axios 1.13.6 → 1.16.1` (exact pin per project convention; clears the ≥1.16.0 advisory floor — prototype-pollution MITM/credential-theft/header-injection, SSRF, ReDoS — after verifying the 1.14–1.17 breaking changes, URL basic-auth decode / parseProtocol strictness / null-proto headers, don't touch this codebase's `axios.create`/interceptor/`isAxiosError` usage). Audit **28 → 1**: only quill 2.0.3 LOW (XSS via HTML-export, CVE-2025-15056) remains — no upstream patch, already mitigated by the existing DOMPurify-on-input + strict allowlist + zero-raw-render in `rich-text-widget.tsx` (and the app never calls Quill's export). Three pre-existing FE bugs surfaced during full-suite verification and were fixed in the same session: (1) `credential-policies-page.handleSave` awaited `form.validateFields()` **outside** its try/catch, so an invalid save escaped as an unhandled promise rejection (a real prod defect, not just test noise) — now caught with early-return; (2) the credential-policies test mock of `notification-bridge` was missing the `appMessage` export; (3) the `smoke-user-pages` test mock of `delegation-api` was missing `useApproveDelegation` (stale since yesterday's `bbbcdcd8` Approve-action slice). The two failures presented as a contention "flake" (the failing file rotated between full-suite runs) but were deterministic stale-mock / unhandled-rejection bugs — isolation peeled them apart. ## Delegation List — Cross-Tenant Scoping Fix (2026-06-10)

**Type:** fix (security, broken-access-control / cross-tenant disclosure — OWASP A01) · `ListDelegationsQuery.cs`, `ListDelegationsQueryHandler.cs`, `DelegationController.cs`, `tests/integration/AqtCoreFW.Identity.Integration.Tests/ListDelegationsQueryTests.cs`.

Closes `DELEG-LIST-OWNERSHIP-SCOPE`, the harvest half of the revoke broken-access-control vector. Empirical scout resolved the filed open question: `UserDelegation` has **no TenantId column and no RLS policy**, so the `sp_set_session_context TenantId` that `DapperReadDbConnection` sets is a no-op for this table — `GET /api/v1/delegations` returned **every delegation across every tenant** (plus soft-deleted rows, since the Dapper query bypasses EF's global filter) to any authenticated caller. The FE `useDelegations` hook sends no owner filter, so the `/delegations` page actually exhibited the leak, not just the API. Severity was higher than originally filed (cross-tenant, not in-tenant). Fix (Model C, query-level scoping — no schema/migration change): `ListDelegationsQuery` gains `ActorId` + `IsPrivileged`; the controller computes `isPrivileged = User.IsInRole(SystemAdmin) || User.IsInRole(Admin)` (same role-claim mechanism as `HttpContextTenantContext`); the handler forces a non-privileged caller to `(DelegatorId=@me OR DelegateId=@me)` and drops the admin-only DelegatorId/DelegateId filters for them, while a privileged caller is tenant-bound via `EXISTS([identity].AspNetUsers WHERE Id IN (DelegatorId, DelegateId) AND (TenantId=@T OR TenantId IS NULL))` (no TenantId column → bind through the parties' user rows, on either party per the chosen variant; NULL-tenant escape hatch matches the codebase RLS convention). `d.IsDeleted = 0` is now unconditional. Build 0W/0E (warn-as-error); integration tests 6/6 (added non-privileged ownership, soft-deleted exclusion, and a privileged tenant-bind test that proves a tenant-B row stays hidden even when its delegator is explicitly requested); code-review APPROVE, 0 blocking. A cross-tenant delegation (delegator in A, delegate in B) is visible to both tenants' admins by the OR-bind — intended per the chosen semantics.

**Type:** fix (security + hygiene) · `OpenIddictDataSeeder.cs`, `RevokeDelegationCommandHandler.cs`, `DelegationController.cs`, `ApproveDelegationCommandHandler.cs` (docstring), `tests/unit/AqtCoreFW.Identity.Application.Tests/Commands/RevokeDelegationCommandHandlerTests.cs`.

## Identity Privilege-Escalation — Red-Team Audit + Fix (3 Critical + H-A) (2026-06-10)

**Type:** fix (security) · `83425d02` (3 Criticals) + `b3f36496` (H-A) · 5 controllers + 5 handlers across `AqtCoreFW.Identity.{Presentation,Application,Infrastructure}` + 6 test files.

A `/ck-security` red-team audit (4 personas) of AuthServer + Identity surfaced broken function-level authorization; 3 Criticals verified against source and fixed: **C1** — 5 admin controllers (PolicyRules/CredentialPolicies/SodRules/Abac/Groups) gated their WRITE endpoints on `.View` only (the matching `.Manage` perms existed but were unused) → 17 write endpoints now `[Authorize(.Manage)]`. **C2** — `AssignRole`/`SyncUserRoles` handlers granted any role with no guard, letting an `IDENTITY.ROLE.MANAGE` holder self-assign the name-based super-role "SystemAdmin" → guard added requiring a SystemAdmin actor, keyed on the role **name** (`Roles.SystemAdmin`/`Admin`) as well as `RoleType.System` because `OpenIddictDataSeeder` seeds those roles defaulted to `Business`, which would have made a RoleType-only guard inert. **C3** — `DelegateRoleCommandHandler` let an Admin set an arbitrary `delegatorId` and auto-activate, granting itself a SystemAdmin's full role set → on-behalf delegations now require approval, and `ApproveDelegationCommandHandler` was hardened (approver must be the delegator or a SystemAdmin, and never the requester or delegate — 4-eyes; the first-order "require approval" fix alone was defeatable by self-approval). **H-A** (review-surfaced 4th path) — `AssignRoleToGroupCommandHandler` could attach a System role to a group (members inherit) → same name-based guard added; code-review grep-confirmed `GroupRoleAssignments.Add` has a single call-site (no bypass). ## Workflow Definition Version Lifecycle — WF-CLONE-AFTER-DELETED-VERSION-500 Closed (2026-06-10)

**Type:** fix (BE / Workflow) · commit `375d682f`.

`/cook WF-CLONE-AFTER-DELETED-VERSION-500` interactive. Two version-lifecycle defects (SQL-verified on the seeded `demo-parallel-process`), fixed with no migration (user chose Option A):

- **Clone version collision (500):** `WorkflowDefinition.Clone()` set `Version = source.Version + 1`. The `(TenantId, DefinitionKey, Version)` unique index is not IsDeleted-filtered, so a soft-deleted version still occupies its number — cloning v1 when a soft-deleted v2 existed recomputed 2 and collided → 500. Clone now takes an explicit `nextVersion = MAX(version) over all rows incl soft-deleted + 1` via new `GetMaxVersionByKeyAsync` (`IgnoreQueryFilters`, tenant-scoped). Versions monotonic, never reused.
- **Delete leaves no latest:** `DeleteWorkflowDefinitionCommandHandler` only soft-deleted. Deleting the latest version left the key with zero latest rows. Delete now promotes the highest surviving (non-deleted) version to `IsLatest`, wrapped with the soft-delete in one `TransactionScope` (new `MarkLatest` + `GetHighestSurvivingByKeyAsync`).
- **Verification:** Workflow Application + Infrastructure build 0W/0E · 7/7 integration (3 new version-lifecycle facts + 3 existing clone deep-copy + existing delete-by-PublicId) · code-review APPROVE 0C/0H/0M (1 Low applied — concurrent-clone race comment; race is pre-existing and the unique index is the correct serializer). Dev-DB seed `Demo Parallel Process` v1 IsLatest repaired (clone of the seed works again).
- **Contract:** no API/schema change (clone/delete endpoints + responses unchanged — behavior fixed). New intra-module repo methods `GetMaxVersionByKeyAsync` + `GetHighestSurvivingByKeyAsync`; `Clone(gen, createdBy)` → `Clone(gen, createdBy, nextVersion)` (single caller).

## Parallel-Branch Visual Designer Declutter — Edge Routing + Dagre Layout (2026-06-09)

**Type:** feature (FE / UX) · web visual designer (React Flow) · commit `96892199` · pushed origin+bitbucket.

- **Root cause (not layout — the dominant visible cause):** `buildGatewayEdges` declared no `sourceHandle`/`targetHandle` → React Flow fell back to the first-declared `Top`/`Bottom` handles → vertical detours on a horizontal left→right flow = the swooping crossings. Edges also had no `type` → bezier, inconsistent with the transitions' smoothstep. **A layout engine alone does NOT fix this** — dagre repositions nodes but never chooses handles; the handle fix is mandatory in every scenario.

Opt-in via the toolbar "Tự động sắp xếp" button; coordinates persist through the normal save path. Auto-layout now re-frames the canvas (`fitView`).
- **DRY:** exported `DIAMOND_SIZE` as the single source of truth for the fork bounding box (was hard-synced).
- **Verification:** tsc 0 errors · 39 related unit tests green (gateway 14 + new dagre-layout 6 + canvas persist/connect + violation) · code-review APPROVE 0C/0H · visual-verified live on `demo-parallel-process`. 2 test-mock regressions self-caught + fixed (`@xyflow/react` full-mock missing `MarkerType` → string literal + `import type`; missing `useReactFlow` → added to mock). ## WF Parallel-Branch RB5 Live-Claimant Gate at Activation (prod fix) — WF-PARALLEL-RB5-RESOLVE-TO-CLAIMANT (T3, 2026-06-08)

**Type:** fix (security/correctness, prod — Workflow.Application graph validator) · **Committed + pushed origin+bitbucket** (ahead=0).

- **`/cook WF-PARALLEL-RB5-RESOLVE-TO-CLAIMANT --auto`.** Closes the prod-fix carved from the negative-path audit: RB5-Activate previously only checked a branch child has a clause of a claimable mode (ByPermission/ByRole), NOT that the pool resolves to ≥1 real claimant. A ByRole pool on a role no active user holds activated clean → forked at runtime → child task unclaimable (403) → AND-join could never complete → instance silently stranded InProgress.
- **Fix:** `WorkflowGraphValidator.ValidateForActivateAsync` gains a live-identity claimant hop — for each branch child whose claimable clauses are **exclusively ByRole**, it resolves the role codes via the existing `IIdentityModuleClient.ResolveActiveUsersInRolesAsync(codes, tenantId)`; 0 active claimants → RB5 violation (422 at activation, def stays inactive). The check is the DIRECT-AspNetUserRoles reverse of the claim-side `GetUserRoleCodesAsync` (PQ-1 A) — code-review verified both SQLs are direct-only, so "resolves to nobody at activate" ⟺ "no user can claim at runtime."
- **🔴 Scope boundary (deliberate, advisor + code-review verified):** ByPermission pools are NOT checked (no reverse permission→users lookup — that is the deferred `WF-NEXT-HANDLER-PERMISSION-USERS` epic); a child with ANY ByPermission clause is conservatively skipped (no false-reject). Empty-refs ByRole → left to the existing runtime fork-entry empty-pool guard. `AllowAssignorOverride` not consulted (the branch-child override guard is an unwired later phase → 0-claimant is unrecoverable today; code notes the future `&& !AllowAssignorOverride`). Activate-only (Save unchanged); a role drained AFTER activation re-opens the deadlock → deferred H1 reconciler is the runtime backstop.
- **Tests:** NEW unit `WorkflowGraphValidatorBranchClaimantRulesTests` (6 facts: ByRole held→pass / unheld→RB5-names-role / lowercase→canonicalizes-before-resolve / ByPermission→skip+DidNotReceive / mixed→skip) — the SUCCESS branch is only provable at the unit layer (integration synthetic users have no real AspNetUserRoles rows). Rewrote integration `ForkChildPoolWithUnheldRole_*` → `…IsRejectedAtActivation` (asserts 422 + RB5 reason names role + def inactive — non-vacuous). Seed gained `SeedSavedParallelDefinitionAsync` (create+save, no activate; DRY refactor).
- **Verification:** Build 0W/0E. Unit 59/59. Integration NegativeTests 3/3. RuntimeTests 3/4 — the 1 fail is the pre-existing documented `WFE-RATELIMIT-TEST-DISABLE` 429 flake (a ByPermission happy-path ClaimAsync, unrelated to ByRole activation validation; the 3 passing Runtime facts confirm no-false-reject for ByPermission). Code-review APPROVE_WITH_CONCERNS, 0 Crit / 0 High (Low-1 malformed-JSON→clean-RB5 applied; Low-2 N+1 accepted — true batching needs an absent coverage-resolver; Info-1 identity-down fail-closed is intended).

## WF Parallel-Branch Runtime ENGINE — P4 of 7 (T5 EPIC, 2026-06-07)

**Scope:** Phase 4 of the parallel-branch runtime epic — the runtime ENGINE that makes a fork actually fire, pool/claim its children, and complete its AND-join atomically. `/cook P4` interactive (FULL engine). One commit `da37f56f` (committed, not yet pushed). Intra-Workflow only — no migration / entity / contract / FE / cross-module change. build 0W/0E · WF.Application 631/631 · WF.Infrastructure 89/89. 2 code-reviews APPROVE_WITH_CONCERNS.

- **Unit 1 — fork-entry gate + candidate fan-out** (closes G2+G4). `ExecuteTransitionCommandHandler`: when a transition target is a branching state, the WF_NO_HANDLER pre-check (which resolves the target's outgoing transitions — none on a fork-only state → false 422) is replaced by a per-child pool resolve via `IWorkflowHandlerResolver.ResolveAssignmentAsync`; **RT4 fail-CLOSED** if ANY child pool is empty AND has no default assignee (would deadlock the AND-join). Pools resolved once, hoisted, handed to `IParallelBranchService.InitiateBranchingAsync` (signature gains `childPools` + `createdBy`) which writes `WorkflowTaskCandidateIndex` + `CandidateRefsJson` per child task (pool-priority over `DefaultAssigneeId` — RT8, no double-surface; RT12 Domain `CreateForStaging`, real tenant/actor). **RT1 fork-exit guard:** any `ExecuteTransition` is rejected while the instance has an `InProgress` branch (single-active-branch). RT11 eager-load was already in place from P1.
- **Unit 2 — atomic join completion** (RT2 + RT3 merged). NEW `IBranchJoinCompletionService` / `BranchJoinCompletionService` (Application.Services, DI in `WorkflowApplicationModule`); the 3 resolution entry points (`ResolveBranchChildCommandHandler` explicit + `CompleteTaskCommandHandler`/`CancelTaskCommandHandler` auto-resolve) now route through it. **Fixes a real strand + silent-failure class:** the 2 auto-resolve callers previously lacked the continuation pre-check AND swallowed the join result, so a join could advance to a handler-less continuation and silently strand. `CompleteJoinAsync` does the continuation pre-check read-only BEFORE the tx (the deterministic fail-CLOSED), then an atomic `{ MarkResolved + ApplyParallelJoinTransition + stage continuation work item }` in one SaveChanges (Slice-7 deferred-save tx envelope). `MarkResolved` moved out of `ParallelBranchService.ResolveBranchChildAsync` into this atomic block — the branch `RowVersion` is the **winner-election token** (a losing concurrent sibling resolves to a clean no-op, not a stranded instance). The child resolution still commits separately (sibling visibility — folding it into the uncommitted tx would deadlock AND-joins under READ COMMITTED). **Contract (user decision):** a join-completion failure on a task action does NOT fail the user's complete/cancel — it is loud-logged for an async reconciler.
- **Carry-forward → P5:** end-to-end fork integration test (activate→Submit→fork→claim→resolve×2→join→continuation); name the two-sibling concurrent-join + background-job-vs-join races as required integration scenarios; async reconciler (`BranchTimeoutCheckerJob` extension: `InProgress` branch with all children resolved but instance not advanced → complete the join; + skip SLA auto-timeout while a branch is InProgress) — blocking-before-prod, but the path is not production-reachable yet (zero parallel definitions in prod).

**Next:** P5 e2e + concurrency coverage + reconciler; 🛑 checkpoint; then P6 claim bridge, P7 demo seed.

Production effect: every tenant collapsed into the `"anon"` namespace, defeating the documented per-tenant scoping. Both fixed to `tenant_id ?? tenantId ?? "anon"` (matches the established defensive pattern; legacy fallback preserved so existing unit tests stay green). The `IdempotencyMiddleware` case was the **higher-severity twin** (surfaced by code-review): on cache-hit it returns the cached 2xx **response body**, so the collapse was a potential cross-tenant data leak (24h TTL, caller-chosen keys) — not just a spurious 409.

**Tests (test-only — no prod entity/contract/migration):** `BpMultiRunHttpTests` gains 3 double-submit facts (same token → 2nd 409 + instance count==1; distinct tokens → both 200 + 2 runs; same token across 2 tenants → both 200 = per-tenant regression-lock for the AntiDoubleSubmit fix) + 1 idempotency fact (same `X-Idempotency-Key` across 2 tenants → distinct definitions, no cached-body leak = regression-lock for the Idempotency fix). DRY: extracted `CreateAndActivateBpAsync` + `BuildWorkflowDefPayload` + token/key POST helpers; Fact 1 refactored onto the shared helper (behavior-preserved).

**Validation:** build 0E/0W · `BpMultiRunHttpTests` 5 PASS / 1 skip (pre-existing AC3) / 0 fail (real SQL2022 + Redis) · `AntiDoubleSubmitMiddlewareTests` 14/14 · `IdempotencyMiddlewareTests` 3/3 (legacy-fallback regression check) · code-review APPROVE_WITH_CONCERNS → M1 (the Idempotency twin) fixed in-scope. ## v2.137p157 — Fix: allow N concurrent BP runs via per-run DossierId (2026-06-06)

**Commits:** `2f5f80bd` (feat, SHIPPED, pushed origin + bitbucket, ahead=0) + `d8ac8f74` (incidental contract-test build-fix).

A second `POST /business-processes/{id}/runs` for the same BusinessProcess returned 500 (`GOV_SYS_000`). Root cause: the unique active-entity index `UX_WorkflowInstances_Active_Entity` `(EntityType, EntityId, TenantId) WHERE CompletedAt IS NULL` + the FE sending `entityId=bpId` permitted only one active run per BP, and `WorkflowInstanceRepository.SaveChangesAsync` translated only `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` so the raw 2601 bubbled to 500.

**Fix (Option B' — per-run DossierId):**
- **Domain/EF:** `WorkflowInstance` gains nullable `DossierId Guid?`; `Create` gains a trailing optional `dossierId` (no `?? entityId` default). Index filter narrowed to `[CompletedAt] IS NULL AND [DossierId] IS NULL` — non-BP rows leave DossierId NULL → still indexed (one-active-per-entity preserved byte-identical, OUTBOX-1 untouched); BP runs mint a non-null DossierId → excluded → N concurrent runs. entityId stays = bpId (FE display-name contract unchanged).
- **Mint:** `StartBusinessProcessRunCommandHandler` injects `IGuidGenerator` and mints `DossierId = gen.NewIdMonotonic()` unconditionally on the BP path — no `"BusinessProcess"` literal anywhere, so the fix is literal-drift-proof. `CreateInstanceByInternalIdAsync` (BP-exclusive prod caller) + `CreateWorkflowInstanceRequest` gain an additive-nullable DossierId (backward compatible).
- **Migration `20260606083540_AddWorkflowInstanceDossierIdAndScopeActiveIndex`:** Up adds the column + drops/recreates the index; **Down is fail-loud** (user-chosen) — THROWs a clear message if any `(EntityType, EntityId, TenantId)` has >1 active run rather than surfacing a raw 1505; never destroys run data. No backfill (existing rows get DossierId NULL → stay indexed; the legacy active BP row sits alone).
- **Layer-1 defense:** `SaveChangesAsync` now also catches `DbUpdateException` wrapping `SqlException` 2601/2627 **scoped to the active-entity index name** → `Result.Fail` new code `GOV_WFL_020` (HTTP 409). Never fires on the BP path (BP rows excluded); guards the non-BP/Generic create race; unrelated unique collisions still bubble.
- **FE:** `new-bp-run-wizard.tsx` mints a per-attempt `X-Request-Token` on StartRun (hand-wired `useStartBpRun` mutation, since the Orval hook has no per-call header) → the registered `AntiDoubleSubmitMiddleware` (`Program.cs:674`, 5s TTL) 409s an accidental re-fire; the wizard surfaces 409 as a friendly toast (reads the normalized flat `status`).

**Validation:** full solution build 0E/0W · 10 real-SQL integration tests PASS (BP double-run distinct DossierId; DB-level B' both directions; Layer-1 GOV_WFL_020 via the EF path; migration coexistence; Down fail-loud guard) + 6 BP unit PASS + preflight index constants synced to B'. Code-review **APPROVE_WITH_CONCERNS** → HIGH-1 (FE read `error.response.status` on the normalized flat error → 409 toast was dead code) + MEDIUM-1 (Layer-1 guard matched 2601/2627 by number only → could mislabel an unrelated unique collision) both fixed + re-verified. **AC6 descoped:** the automated BE-integration test for the double-submit token — the WebApplicationFactory harness does not wire AntiDoubleSubmit/Redis; the production path is verified by inspection (middleware registered + reads the header + FE sends it). Follow-up `BP-DOUBLE-SUBMIT-TOKEN-BE-TEST`.

**depmap:** entity-graph + index-filter + contract notes updated. **Incidental:** `WorkflowApiContractTests` (red on `main` since v2.137p155 — missing `Branches` arg on `WorkflowDefinitionDto`) fixed in `d8ac8f74` to restore a green full-solution build.

## v2.137p154 — Feat: auto-claim on transition execute + ownership gate (workflow work items) (2026-06-04)

**Type:** feat (BE workflow authz + FE) | **Scope:** 1 BE handler + 3 FE files + tests | **Status:** IMPLEMENTED (local, uncommitted) — unit-verified + review-approved; integration deferred (live API DLL lock); pending API restart + in-browser confirm before commit.

**The change:** A BP-run page showed both a transition action ("Xem xét") and a pool claim ("Nhận việc") at once because execute authz was eligibility-only and ignored claim ownership — any eligible user could advance a task another had claimed, so "Nhận việc" gave no real exclusivity. Adopted **auto-claim on act + ownership gate**:

- **BE `ExecuteTransitionCommandHandler`:** when advancing a state, the open work item is (a) rejected with `AlreadyClaimed` (GOV_WFL_016, 409) if claimed by ANOTHER user — an additional layer *after* the existing eligibility authz; (b) auto-claimed to the acting user if unclaimed; then completed. Single authoritative read of the task inside the transaction; foreign-claim reject mirrors the existing rollback + ClearChanges idiom. Recall path unchanged. Concurrency: two racers serialize on the task `RowVersion` + instance `CurrentStateId` concurrency token → loser gets a clean 409 StateConflict, no lost update. BP ambient-tx caller observes the Fail and rolls back its own uow.
- **FE:** `AllowedActionsBar` hides transition buttons (showing "đã giao cho X") when the work item is claimed by another user, so the user never dead-clicks into the 409 (gated until transitions + tasks + current user id are all loaded). `NextHandlerCard` offers "Trả việc" (unclaim) when the task is claimed by the current user. New `useUnclaimTask` hook (existing `POST /workflow/tasks/:id/unclaim`).

**Model:** claim = "reserve for later" (ownership without acting); transition = "act now" (auto-claims if unclaimed). The two affordances coexist meaningfully instead of redundantly.

**Verification:** BE Workflow.Application 603 + 3 new ownership-gate unit tests (auto-claim / self-claim / foreign-reject) + 10 BP transition tests pass; FE tsc 0E. Code-review APPROVED (0 Crit/High/Med; tx/rollback own+ambient, concurrency serialization, 409-vs-403, FE sub/assigneeId convention all verified against live code). **Integration tests not run** (the running dev API holds the workflow DLLs — rebuild blocked; covered by unit + review, deferred to a clean run after API restart).

**No migration/entity/contract/endpoint change** (reuses existing unclaim endpoint). No dependency-map change.

## v2.137p153 — Fix: permission-deny on [RequiresMfa] endpoint mislabeled as 2FA step-up (BP-run redirect) (2026-06-04)

**Type:** fix (BE auth + FE resilience) | **Scope:** 2 BE handlers + 1 shared evaluator, 6 FE files | **Status:** SHIPPED (local main `cbe92117`) — unit-verified + in-browser confirmed (BP-run page renders, no 2FA redirect) after API restart.

**The bug:** A GovOfficer opening `/business-process-runs/{id}` was redirected to the 2FA screen. `NextHandlerCard` fires cosmetic label-lookup calls to admin endpoints (`GET /admin/roles`, `/admin/permissions`, `/admin/org/units`). `RolesAdminController` carries `[Authorize(IDENTITY.ROLE.VIEW)]` + `[RequiresMfa]`; GovOfficer lacks `IDENTITY.ROLE.VIEW` (DB-confirmed: 31 perms, none = ROLE.VIEW) → 403 by **permission**. But `MfaForbidResultHandler` stamped `X-Mfa-Required` whenever the combined endpoint policy merely **contained** an `MfaRequirement` (not whether MFA was the failed requirement) → FE `api-client` redirected to `/account/mfa`. A permission-deny was thus mislabeled as an MFA step-up — deterministic, timing-independent (re-login does not help; GovOfficer still lacks the perm). Phase 7's instance-view re-gate (commit `1e04a026`) did not cause this — it *exposed* it by letting the page render `NextHandlerCard`.

**BE fix (the systemic correctness):**
- New `MfaClaimEvaluator.IsMfaRecent(user, maxAgeHours)` — shared recency check.
- `MfaRequirementHandler` delegates to it (behavior preserved; 6 existing tests green).
- `MfaForbidResultHandler` emits `X-Mfa-Required` **only when** an `MfaRequirement` is present **and** `!IsMfaRecent` (MFA genuinely unmet). The failed-requirements set is unreliable here — the requirement handler signals via `context.Fail()` → `ExplicitFail()` with an empty failed-requirements collection — so the claim is re-derived. Permission-deny + fresh MFA → plain 403 (forbidden toast), not a 2FA redirect.

**FE fix (operational page must not be hijacked by cosmetic lookups):**
- `api-client.ts`: axios `suppressAuthInterstitial` flag → 403 on flagged requests skips ALL interstitials/redirects/toasts and rejects.
- `query-config.ts`: `QueryCache.onError` honors `meta.suppressErrorToast` (the axios flag can't reach react-query's global onError — otherwise up to 4 stacked "load failed" toasts).
- `useRoles`/`usePermissions`/`useWorkflowOrgUnits`/`useUserGroups` accept `{ background: true }` → set both flags; `NextHandlerCard` passes it on all 4 lookups (existing `resolveLabel` already falls back to raw ref).

**Verification:** BE build 0E/0W (Identity.Infrastructure + Api host); MFA unit 20/20 (6 preserved + 6 new `MfaForbidResultHandlerTests` + 8 policy-provider); FE tsc 0E; api + core/api suites 84/84 (incl. 2 new api-client-mfa cases + 4 new query-config onError cases). 12 unrelated FE files fail but proven pre-existing flaky (fail *more* on clean HEAD via git stash; set includes pure-util base64 tests). **NOT yet verified end-to-end in browser** (running API still holds the pre-fix binary; needs rebuild+restart).

**No migration/entity/contract/endpoint/job change.** `X-Mfa-Required` header semantics refined, wire format unchanged. No dependency-map change.

BE `FormTemplateVersionFactory` now serializes each field's static options (`OptionPayload` = Id/Value/LabelVi/LabelEn/DisplayOrder, sorted by DisplayOrder) as an **additive-nullable** `Options` key on `FieldPayload` (`SchemaEnvelopeVersion` held at 1, following the PrefillSource precedent). FE adapter maps `f.options` → `FormFieldDto.options` (String(id) normalize). `renderInteractiveField` EnumRef case already reads inline `field.options` → Select now renders choices.

**End-to-end chain (scout + code-review both verified independently):** producer repo `GetByPublicIdWithFieldsAsync` eager-loads `.ThenInclude(f=>f.Options)` → all 3 BP query handlers (intake/state/transition) pass raw `snapshot.SchemaJson` through unchanged (no re-serialize strip) → zero `UnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow` in `src` so every reader (prefill resolver, etc.) ignores the new key safely → FE renderer reads inline. Submission validation reads LIVE `template.Fields`, not the snapshot → unaffected.

**Backward-compat:** old snapshots without an `options` key parse to `null` (verified non-vacuously both sides). Existing Active templates keep optionless snapshots until republished — the shared `Snapshot()` factory self-heals on next (re)publish; no backfill migration (YAGNI). **Known dev caveat:** `DemoFormTemplateSeeder`'s already-seeded `muc_do_uu_tien` EnumRef snapshot is optionless until the next `reset-all` (which regenerates it with options). No prod template currently affected.

**No migration / no entity / no public-API / no new endpoint.** Build: BE `FormTemplateVersionFactoryTests` 9/9 + full `Forms.Domain.Tests` 132/132 · FE `tsc --noEmit` 0E + `form-snapshot-adapter.test` 5/5 + full FE forms suite 201/201 · code-review APPROVE 0 Crit/High/Med. ## v2.137p146 — Fix: diacritic-insensitive address-widget province/ward search (2026-06-03)

**Type:** fix (FE search UX) | **Scope:** new `foldDiacritics` shared util + `address-field-widget` filterOption + util test | **Status:** SHIPPED (local main). Closes `GEO-WIDGET-FILTER-ACCENT-INSENSITIVE` (T4).

**The change:** after v2.137p145 seeded all 34 provinces (up to ~166 wards each) into the address widget, its `filterOption` (`address-field-widget.tsx:52`) used raw `.toLowerCase().includes()` — diacritic-sensitive, so typing "nghe" would not match "Nghệ An" nor "phuong" any "Phường …". New `foldDiacritics()` (`shared/utils/fold-diacritics.ts`) folds both input + label before compare: lowercase → NFD → strip combining marks (U+0300–U+036F, incl. horn for ư/ơ + dot-below) → map `đ`→`d` (U+0111 has no NFD decomposition, the silent-trap) → trim. Applied to both province + ward Selects; exact-match behavior preserved.

**Verification:** `fold-diacritics.test.ts` 14/14 vitest — one case per Unicode trap category (đ, horn, dot-below, breve, hook-above, tilde, uppercase, null/empty, search-match contract) so a future range-narrowing "simplification" flips a case red instead of regressing silently. `tsc --noEmit` 0E. code-review APPROVE 0 Crit/High.

**Scope discipline:** util built reusable but applied ONLY to the address widget the row named. ~13 other Selects (users/roles/orgunits/ref-fields) filter small/non-geographic lists where accent-sensitivity is tolerable. One genuine same-scale sibling — `master-data-page.tsx:159,171` (admin province/district CRUD, also 34-province) — filed as fast-follow `MASTERDATA-PAGE-FILTER-ACCENT-INSENSITIVE`, not bundled (YAGNI). FE-only; no BE/contract/migration/entity change → no dependency-map update.

## v2.137p143 — Fix: transaction-wrap the multi-SaveChanges demo workflow + form-template seeders (2026-06-02)

**Type:** fix (seeding crash-safety) | **Scope:** DemoWorkflowSeeder + DemoFormTemplateSeeder (2 files, +16 lines) | **Status:** SHIPPED (local main).

**Gap closed:** `DemoWorkflowSeeder` (3-phase: def+states → transitions → ByRole assignments) and `DemoFormTemplateSeeder` (2-phase: template+fields+options → publish+snapshot) each issued multiple `SaveChangesAsync` with NO enclosing transaction. A mid-seed fault on a live DB could leave a committed root (def / Draft template) with missing children that the root-keyed idempotency probe — Workflow `(TenantId, DefinitionKey)`, Forms `(TenantId, Code)` — then skips forever on a plain restart (never repaired). `reset-all` nukes first and self-heals; a live-DB crash would not.

**Fix:** wrap each seeder's phases in a single `BeginTransactionAsync`/`CommitAsync` (begin after the existence-probe early-return, commit after the last SaveChanges), mirroring the already-shipped `DemoBusinessProcessSeeder` (P6). The probe + read stay outside the tx (no transaction held across the no-op skip path); the per-tenant transaction is scoped inside the static seed method so one tenant's failure can't roll back another's. Brings P4 + P5 to txn-wrap parity with P6/P7c/P7a/P7b.

**Verified safe:** no `EnableRetryOnFailure` / retrying execution strategy on either prod registration (`WorkflowInfrastructureModule.cs:39`, `FormsInfrastructureModule.cs:26` configure only `MigrationsHistoryTable`), so the manual `BeginTransactionAsync` cannot hit the "strategy does not support user-initiated transactions" throw.

**No migration / no entity change / no public-contract change** (static method signatures unchanged → existing tests compile + call them directly). Build slnx 0E/0W. `DemoWorkflowSeederTests` 4/4 + `DemoFormTemplateSeederTests` 4/4 green (real SQL via SqlServerCollection/WebAppFixture — the new tx path is genuinely exercised). Code-review APPROVE 0 Crit/High/Med/Low.

**Accepted (unchanged from P6):** transaction-rollback + StartAsync boot path not fault-injection-tested. Manual reset-all smoke still owed via `WF-DEMO-SEED-SMOKE`.
